title: US Open 2026: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz return in mixed doubles
author: Harry Poole; Russell Fuller
content:
![Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz laugh together during the US Open mixed doubles competition](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/6c61/live/244bbbd0-a0d4-11f1-879c-376a9fd2230d.jpg)
Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz have won a combined 30 Grand Slam singles titles
- Published
Enjoy it - and do what Serena Williams tells you to.
That was how Carlos Alcaraz settled back into competitive action at the US Open, partnering the American great as she returned to her home slam after a four-year absence.
The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format has attracted criticism for favouring the allure of the sport's top singles stars at the expense of established doubles players.
But the crowds turned out and produced a terrific atmosphere for the tournament's headline act, with about 15,000 people packed inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
All four doubles specialist pairings lost to a team of singles players on Tuesday, while Alcaraz and Williams fell in the quarter-finals.
Seven-time major winner Alcaraz was playing his first competitive match since April after injuring his wrist, while 23-time Grand Slam champion Williams was competing in New York for the first time since she "evolved away" from tennis in 2022.
The pair were greeted by huge cheers and were roared on throughout their opening 5-3 4-1 win against Great Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe.
The 44-year-old Williams won the US Open mixed doubles title in its original format alongside Max Mirnyi in 1998 - five years before Alcaraz was born.
Almost 30 years later, Williams still had the competitive desire. She and Alcaraz enjoyed the occasion, playing with smiles on their faces and roaring each other on after winning a point.
Interviewed during a change of ends, Alcaraz said: "I'm playing next to the one and only Serena Williams, so what else can I do? Just enjoy and try to do the things she told me to do."
Their partnership improved rapidly in their first match as they won eight of the final nine games to seal victory.
However, they were denied a place in Wednesday's semi-finals by Italy's world number six Flavio Cobolli and Swiss team-mate Belinda Bencic, who won 5-4 (7-4) 4-1.
Returning Alcaraz 'almost forgot how this feels'
While Williams will not contest the singles at the US Open - she has not competed in that format since injuring her knee at Wimbledon - Tuesday's matches provided the returning Alcaraz with valuable court time.
The Spaniard admitted he felt nervous before stepping out on the court - in part due to partnering six-time US Open women's singles champion Williams.
"I think everyone could see I was really nervous, I double-faulted on the first point," Alcaraz said after their opening win.
"I was out for almost five months and I almost forgot how it feels stepping out on the court once again.
"It [took] just a couple of games [to settle] and she made it very easy for me to enjoy it and try to go for it."
For Williams, a return to the Arthur Ashe Stadium was something she did not believe would come around again.
"It's always amazing to be here. I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said.
"It was just a really cool moment. I never thought this would happen."
![Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz are applauded by the crowd at the US Open](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/a08d/live/adae41c0-a0d6-11f1-b407-c570883a85b8.jpg)
Serena Williams won six of her 23 Grand Slam singles titles in New York
The controversial revamped mixed doubles format, introduced last year, pits established doubles players against some of the sport's biggest singles stars.
The tournament takes place the week before the singles draw gets under way and allows direct entry into the main draw for top-ranked singles players and wildcards.
Established doubles players such as Britons Glasspool and Henry Patten had to come through two qualifying rounds on Monday.
Top-ranked players Patten and Katerina Siniakova advanced to the quarter-finals before losing to husband-and-wife duo Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina.
Discussing their dynamic, with a semi-final against Cobolli and Bencic to come, Frenchman Monfils said: "I'm a big fan of her game and mentality. Sometimes I think she's ice and I'm the fire.
"We needed to the find the balance. We did today."
The other semi-final will see Russians Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev face Czech pair Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik.
It was not all plain sailing for the leading singles players, with men's 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic and women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka suffering an early exit at the hands of Patten and Siniakova.
'The sort of semi-final line-up organisers envisaged'
Sabalenka and Djokovic lasted just 49 minutes, but this was otherwise a day where the singles stars edged out the doubles specialists.
With none of the four doubles pairs making it to the last four, the USTA has the sort of semi-final line up it envisaged when deciding to reinvent the mixed doubles 12 months ago.
Sabalenka and Djokovic turned out to be a very brief experiment. The other marquee pairing of Williams and Alcaraz lasted longer, with Williams in particular catching the eye in their first round win.
But with Alcaraz looking increasingly rusty in the quarter-final, Cobolli and Bencic won convincingly.
The Spaniard was wearing a compression sleeve on his right arm, and the skin fade of earlier in the year has been replaced by a mop of black hair.
This was useful court time for him, but did not really tell us anything about his chances of remaining in New York for the singles final in just under three weeks time.
summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz partnered in the US Open's revamped mixed doubles tournament, drawing a crowd of about 15,000 to Arthur Ashe Stadium. Williams was returning to the tournament for the first time since 2022, while Alcaraz was playing his first match since April due to a wrist injury. The marquee pair won their opening match before being eliminated in the quarter-finals by Flavio Cobolli and Belinda Bencic.
key_points: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz teamed up for the US Open mixed doubles, reaching the quarter-finals.
Carlos Alcaraz was returning from a wrist injury that sidelined him for nearly five months.
Serena Williams played at Flushing Meadows for the first time since stepping away from tennis in 2022.
The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format features top singles stars alongside traditional doubles players.
Williams and Alcaraz were eliminated in the quarter-finals by Italy's Flavio Cobolli and Switzerland's Belinda Bencic.

title: US Open LIVE: Latest scores and updates as Williams and Alcaraz play mixed doubles
author: Flo Clifford
content:
Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles tournament but were knocked out by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.
23-time grand slam champion Williams was competing in New York four years after the final competitive singles match of her career - or at least, the first phase of her career - before she began “evolving away” from the sport.
But the 44-year-old returned to action alongside Spaniard Alcaraz, who had not played in four months due to a troublesome wrist injury - but is back to defend his singles title at Flushing Meadows.
Elsewhere in the high-profile but controversial mixed doubles event, which is in its second year after a major revamp, world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka and 24-time grand slam champion Novak Djokovic were made top seeds but were knocked out in the first round by Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten.
Follow all the action with our liveblog below:
Bencic/Cobolli see off Williams/Alcaraz
Another entertaining encounter goes the way of the fourth seeds.
So our semi-final line-ups are almost set:
Belinda Bencic/Flavio Cobolli v Elina Svitolina/Gael Monfils
Karolina Muchova/Jakub Mensik v Mirra Andreeva/Andrey Rublev OR Diana Shnaider/Casper Ruud
![](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/25/23/2026-08-25T220314Z_1573894166_UP1EM8P1P9CCB_RTRMADP_3_TENNIS-USOPEN.JPG)
GAME, SET AND MATCH! Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 4-1 Williams/Alcaraz
Alcaraz goes long on the return, and the smiles finally come out for Bencic and Cobolli!
They’re into the semi-finals, where they’ll face Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils.
Smiles too for Williams and Alcaraz, who have shaken some of the rust off with those two matches today.
*Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 3-1 Williams/Alcaraz
So, Cobolli will face for a place in the semi-finals. Bencic knocks a net volley right at Alcaraz’s feet to push him off-balance for 15-0. Then Alcaraz goes wide on a tricky second serve.
Williams nets on a backhand, and that’s four match points...
BREAK! *Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 3-1 Williams/Alcaraz
Very assured by Bencic at the baseline as she trades blows with Alcaraz, before Williams intercepts - but goes long. 15-15 on the Alcaraz serve.
Cobolli reacts brilliantly to lash a Williams drop shot cross-court, leaving Bencic acres of space to hammer in the winner.
Williams gets a smash away for 30-30, but a great return by Cobolli brings up break point chance... an ace saves the first, but they’ll have another.
Ooh, Cobolli reads it well, and Alcaraz goes long!
Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 2-1 Williams/Alcaraz*
Williams is just producing a few more unforced errors than in the earlier match against Routliffe and Glasspool. She nets on a weak Bencic second serve, and Alcaraz slams the tape too under pressure from Cobolli.
The Italian lets a Williams volley drop and waits, then plants it into the open court.
*Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 1-1 Williams/Alcaraz
Williams smiles ruefully as she nets and a chorus of support comes up from Arthur Ashe. The decibels from the American have gone up too.
From 0-30 down Alcaraz pushes Cobolli back and fires an overhead into the open court, and an ace down the T from Williams gets them to parity.
Cobolli draws the error from Williams in a cross-court rally and that gives them two break points... Bencic is unlucky that a return drifts wide for deuce.
Alcaraz seals the deciding point at the net!
Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 1-0 Williams/Alcaraz*
Cobolli is in a spot of bother on serve but Williams hammers a forehand into the net as the Italian goes up 40-30.
He whacks a forehand into the open court and seals the hold. Both teams are so comfortable at the back of the court.
GAME AND FIRST SET! Bencic/Cobolli 5-4 Williams/Alcaraz
Cobolli smashes away after Bencic pounces on a weaker Williams second serve for 4-4.
And Williams goes long at the baseline! 5-4... Cobolli can serve this out now.
Williams mishits a wild volley and that gives Cobolli two set points!
A kick serve out wide seals it. The pair exchange a businesslike high five. Serious stuff.
Bencic/Cobolli 4-4 Williams/Alcaraz*
Big serving by Cobolli to build a 3-0 lead.
Bencic nets on Alcaraz’s serve... and Williams powers away a smash at the net to close some of the gap.
She does so again, and that lead evaporates. 3-3.
summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles tournament before being knocked out by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli. Williams returned to competition in New York four years after her last competitive singles match, while Alcaraz returned following a four-month wrist injury. In another notable first-round match, top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic were eliminated by Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten.
key_points: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz were defeated in the US Open mixed doubles quarter-finals by Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.
Bencic and Cobolli advanced to the semi-finals to face Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils.
Top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic were knocked out in the first round by Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten.
The tournament marked Williams' return to competitive tennis in New York four years after her final singles match.

title: Leeds player ratings vs Forest as 'assured' debutant gets 8/10 but 'sloppy' 5
author: Kyle Newbould
content:
Leeds United booked their place in the Carabao Cup third round after beating Nottingham Forest 2-0 on Tuesday night. A second-half goal from Daniel James and a Neco Williams own-goal sent Daniel Farke’s side home from the City Ground with a second win in four days.
Chances fell at both ends during the first-half, the biggest for Chris Wood who after nutmegging Nico Elvedi, was primed to finish but for a goal-saving Joe Rodon tackle. Sean Longstaff had Leeds’ best opportunity after James got free down the right, but the midfielder was falling as he shot and a weak effort was collected by Matz Sels.
James opened the scoring six minutes into the second-half, finishing well beyond Sels and into the far corner after Longstaff pounced on some loose Forest play. And Williams put into his own net to double the away side’s lead with around 15 minutes remaining, although James Justin might be trying to claim it as his own.
Here are our Leeds United player ratings from the game...
![7 - A couple of early kicks went out of play. Great save from Wood early in the second-half.](https://www.connachttribune.ie/jpim-static/image/2026/08/24/9/17/GettyImages-2290937503.jpeg?trim=0,190,0,190&crop=&width=800)
![7 - Produced a brilliant goal-saving tackle on Wood. Physical and full of energy down the right.](https://www.connachttribune.ie/jpim-static/image/2026/08/24/9/37/GettyImages-2291547634.jpeg?trim=0,219,0,219&crop=&width=800)
![8 - Looked very assured from kick-off, not at all like someone making their debut. Plenty of good reading of play and decent on the ball too. A great debut.](https://www.connachttribune.ie/jpim-static/image/2026/08/25/19/11/GettyImages-2292029004.jpeg?trim=0,224,0,224&crop=&width=800)
3. CB: Nico Elvedi
8 - Looked very assured from kick-off, not at all like someone making their debut. Plenty of good reading of play and decent on the ball too. A great debut. | Getty Images
![7 - Steady. Some good punchy passes. Header back into a dangerous area led to Justin’s goal.](https://www.connachttribune.ie/jpim-static/image/2026/08/24/9/43/GettyImages-2290959055.jpeg?trim=0,183,0,183&crop=&width=800)
![7 - Got free down the right loads but crossing mixed and missed a good chance. Finished well for the opener though.](https://www.connachttribune.ie/jpim-static/image/2026/08/25/20/20/GettyImages-2292033896.jpeg?trim=0,179,0,179&crop=&width=800)
![7 - Steady away. Won tackles, played mostly simple passes.](https://www.connachttribune.ie/jpim-static/image/2026/08/24/9/37/GettyImages-2291604708.jpeg?trim=0,201,0,201&crop=&width=800)
summary: Leeds United advanced to the Carabao Cup third round with a 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground. Daniel James opened the scoring early in the second half, followed by a second goal resulting from a Neco Williams own-goal. The win marked Daniel Farke's second victory for the side in four days.
key_points: Leeds United defeated Nottingham Forest 2-0 in the Carabao Cup.
Daniel James scored the opening goal six minutes into the second half.
A Neco Williams own-goal doubled Leeds' lead with about 15 minutes remaining.
Joe Rodon made a crucial goal-saving tackle on Chris Wood during the first half.

title: Celtic throw away four-goal aggregate lead to crash out of Champions League against Lask
author: PA Media; Guardian staff reporter
content:
Celtic threw away a four-goal lead in Austria as they missed out on the Champions League for the second year running. The Scottish champions looked to be cruising into the league stage when Callum McGregor put them 4-0 up on aggregate against Lask with a 21st-minute deflected strike.
However, they went on to endure one of their all-time European lows with a 5-1 defeat in Linz delivering a £20m-plus blow.
The Hoops had other chances in the first half but the Austrians gave themselves a lifeline when Moses Usor pounced on a loose pass from Benjamin Nygren to level on the night in the 32nd minute.
The tie began to spiral out of Celtic’s control early in the second half as Robert Ljubicic and Samuel Adeniran netted from outside the box. Martin O’Neill’s side looked like they would cling on but Florian Flecker nodded home from close range in stoppage-time to spark an additional 30 minutes.
Celtic had disappeared as an attacking force at half-time and Adeniran delivered the knockout blow that sends them into the Europa League.
The Hoops exited on penalties at the playoff stage last season after failing to sign a proven striker before drawing a blank against Kairat Almaty. Fans will this year question the decision to sell Arne Engels just ahead of the first leg after they lost control in midfield in Austria.
The quality of Celtic’s finishing had been the difference in Glasgow but Lask created chances throughout and the second leg started in similar fashion.
Celtic looked to extend their lead. Mika Baur stabbed an early chance just wide and Kasper Høgh forced a couple of first-half saves from decent opportunities. McGregor opened the scoring in between those chances when he drilled a first-time shot in off a defender after Yang Hyun-jun had played a one-two with Kieran Tierney.
The home side had exerted some pressure just before McGregor’s goal and they levelled following careless play from Nygren. The Austrian champions pulled a goal back three minutes after the restart when Usor outmuscled Auston Trusty and worked the ball inside for Ljubicic to drive home from 20 yards.
![Dismayed Celtic players react to their capitulation](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/9dae202d24604a80213dda2cac29b8f00d1f617f/0_0_4199_2799/master/4199.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Celtic endured some nervy moments before they conceded again in the 58th minute when Adeniran curled a wonderful first-time strike into the top corner from 25 yards.
after newsletter promotion
Celtic were on the ropes. Several shots flew past Viljami Sinisalo’s goal before the Finn pulled off a great stop from Sascha Horvath. João Victor Tornich headed inches wide from the resulting corner.
Adeniran fired off the underside of the bar and Celtic defended with four centre-backs as Liam Scales and Dane Murray came on to join Trusty and Cameron Carter-Vickers.
With Luke McCowan, Reo Hatate and Sebastian Tounekti also off the bench, Carter-Vickers had to struggle on with cramp and Celtic could not hold out. Sinisalo made a great stop from a Tornich header but Flecker converted the rebound.
Anthony Ralston replaced Carter-Vickers as extra-time allowed O’Neill to make a further change and Celtic appeared to stem the tide. However, Adeniran fired home from 25 yards with five minutes left after dispossessing McCowan and Celtic could not threaten after Sinisalo’s penalty save denied the striker his hat-trick.
summary: Celtic squandered a four-goal aggregate lead to suffer a 5-1 defeat against Lask in Austria, resulting in a Champions League exit. Callum McGregor had initially put Celtic ahead in the 21st minute, but goals from Moses Usor, Robert Ljubicic, Florian Flecker, and two from Samuel Adeniran turned the tie around. The defeat deals a £20m-plus financial blow to Celtic and drops them into the Europa League.
key_points: Celtic lost 5-1 on the night in Linz after holding a 4-0 aggregate lead.
Samuel Adeniran scored two goals for Lask, including the knockout blow in extra time.
Florian Flecker forced extra time by scoring in stoppage time at the end of regulation.
The defeat marks the second consecutive year Celtic has missed out on the Champions League.

title: Manchester United confirm Carlos Baleba signing as midfield spend nears £150m
author: Guardian sport
content:
Manchester United have completed the signing of the Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m. The Cameroon international is the third midfielder to join this summer, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.
Baleba has signed a five-year contract with the option to extend for 12 months after United agreed a £65m deal plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on with Brighton. It takes the club’s spend on midfielders to about £148m.
Santos and Tielemans have arrived from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively during a summer when Casemiro left and Manuel Ugarte sustained a serious knee injury.
“It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams,” Baleba said. “Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.
“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.
“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”
United made a move to bring in Baleba last summer but cooled their pursuit when Brighton made it clear he was not leaving. Baleba was not at his best last season but that did not put off United, who stepped up their interest in the 22-year-old a week ago.
United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, said: “Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further. He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.
after newsletter promotion
“We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.”
summary: Manchester United has completed the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m on a five-year contract. He is the club's third midfield addition of the summer, following Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, bringing United's total summer midfield spending to approximately £148m. The move comes after Casemiro's departure and a serious knee injury to Manuel Ugarte.
key_points: Carlos Baleba signed a five-year contract with an option for an extra 12 months.
The transfer fee is £65m plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on clause.
Baleba joins Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans as United's summer midfield recruits.
The new signings elevate Manchester United's total midfield spending to about £148m.

title: Delap heads to Forest for £50m as Chelsea open talks to sell Jackson to Aston Villa
author: Jacob Steinberg
content:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a deal worth £50m to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea, who have also opened talks over selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa.
Xabi Alonso has made João Pedro and Danny Welbeck his main strikers this season, leaving his other frontmen to seek opportunities elsewhere.
Forest were one of several clubs interested in Delap, who has struggled since joining Chelsea from Ipswich for £30m last summer, and will pay a club record of £45m plus £5m in add-ons for the 23-year-old.
Delap managed only one league goal last season and was hindered by injuries after leaving Ipswich. But the former Manchester City striker was a key target for Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, and has a chance to revive his career at the City Ground.
Chelsea are focused on outgoings before the transfer window shuts next Tuesday and are also hoping to sell Jackson, who was on loan at Bayern Munich last season. The Senegal international is valued at £65m and has been earmarked by Villa as a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.
Chelsea are not willing to agree to another loan for Jackson and want his valuation met but Villa are likely to press for a favourable payment schedule to ensure they can afford a permanent deal. Atlético Madrid are also interested in the 25-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Villarreal in 2023. Unai Emery, Villa’s manager, worked with Jackson at Villarreal.
West Ham’s clear out after relegation from the Premier League is expected to continue with El Hadji Malick Diouf joining Brentford for about £35m. The clubs are in discussions over a deal for the left-back and an agreement is likely soon.
Diouf wants to leave and was left out of the squad when Nuno Espírito Santo’s side continued their disappointing start to the Championship season by losing 2-1 at home against Charlton last Saturday.
West Ham signed the Senegal international for £19m from Slavia Prague last year. Brentford have made four signings and are plan to strengthen further.
after newsletter promotion
Nuno, who is understood to be under growing pressure after West Ham’s flat start, has had his hand weakened by a host of players hoping to force their way out. The Mexico midfielder Edson Álvarez has not been involved in the first two league games and is the subject of interest from Olympiakos and Real Sociedad.
Torino have had a bid rejected for the midfielder Soungoutou Magassa, who is on Crystal Palace’s shortlist. Marseille could sign the French centre-back Jean-Clair Todibo. West Ham have raised funds through the sales of Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts, and have loaned Aaron Wan-Bissaka to Aston Villa and Niclas Füllkrug to Werder Bremen.
summary: Nottingham Forest has agreed to a club-record £50m deal to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea, while Chelsea has also opened talks to sell Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa for £65m. Meanwhile, West Ham continues a player clear-out following their relegation, with El Hadji Malick Diouf in talks to join Brentford for about £35m. Other West Ham players, including Edson Álvarez, are also drawing interest from various clubs as manager Nuno Espírito Santo faces mounting pressure.
key_points: Nottingham Forest agreed to a £50m deal (comprising £45m plus £5m in add-ons) to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea.
Chelsea is in talks to sell Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa for £65m as Villa seeks a replacement for Ollie Watkins.
West Ham left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf is close to joining Brentford for approximately £35m.
West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo is under growing pressure following a poor start in the Championship and multiple players seeking exits.

title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools
author: Adrian Kajumba; Sahil Jaidka
content:
Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools
Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences
Tuesday 25 August 2026 18:34, UK
Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.
Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct.
York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors.
York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.
He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.
Records also show that York had his cell phone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.
Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.
"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email.
"You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offences in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."
The 49ers Enterprises - who are the investment arm of York's San Francisco 49ers - own Leeds United. The Premier League club have declined to comment.
They are also part of the US consortium who acquired a majority shareholding in Rangers last summer. However, York is not listed on the club's list of board members.
When contacted by Sky Sports News, Rangers chose not to comment.
A San Francisco 49ers statement read: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."
The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy.
Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy.
summary: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested on Sunday morning in East Palestine, Ohio. He pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools after prosecutors amended an initial charge of engaging in prostitution. York was sentenced to one day in jail, which was already served, and fined $1,150.
key_points: Jed York was arrested at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio.
He pleaded no contest to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.
Prosecutors amended the original charge of engaging in prostitution.
York received a one-day jail sentence, which was credited as served, and a $1,150 fine.
The NFL stated it is aware of the arrest and will review the matter under its personal conduct policy.

title: Carlos Baleba: Manchester United sign Cameroon midfielder from Brighton in Â£70m deal
author: Paul Battison; Simon Stone; Mohamed Moallim
content:
![Carlos Baleba pictured smiling in a Manchester United shirt](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/9550/live/37514d90-a0a1-11f1-84a9-276d1a8e5a22.jpg)
Carlos Baleba has won 16 caps for Cameroon
- Published
Manchester United have signed Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a Â£70m deal.
The Old Trafford club have paid an initial Â£65m, plus a potential Â£5m in add-ons, for the 22-year-old, while Brighton have negotiated a sell-on clause.
United targeted Baleba after deciding to strengthen their midfield further following the summer arrivals of Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa.
Baleba has signed a five year-contract at Old Trafford, with the option to extend for a further year.
"It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams," he said. "Playing at Old Trafford is always special, but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.
"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.
"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."
Baleba's move follows United's shock 2-0 defeat by Hull City in Saturday's Premier League opener, where Santos and Tielemans made their midfield debuts.
United reignited their interest after attempting to sign him last year near deadline day, but were put off by Brighton's valuation, which was in excess of Â£100m.
Baleba, who joined Brighton from Lille in 2023, is currently sidelined with an ankle injury he picked up during the Seagulls' pre-season training camp in Austria.
He made 112 appearances for Brighton, scoring four times, and 31 in the Premier League last season as they finished eighth to qualify for this season's Conference League.
The move has taken United's summer spending up to Â£153m as they prepare for a return to the Champions League for the first time since the 2023-24 campaign.
'He adds physicality and power'
United will hope for the 2024-25 version of Baleba rather than last season's because it was his performances in that campaign that attracted them.
We can't know what would have happened if the approach for Mateus Fernandes had been successful, nor if Mason Mount had not suffered the injury in the pre-season game with Paris St-Germain two weeks ago that ruled him out of the Premier League opener.
However, even before Saturday's disappointing loss at Hull it is clear that, despite adding Santos and Tielemans to their midfield ranks, they still lack physicality and power.
In theory, Baleba should solve that issue.
The 22-year-old is strong in possession, covers ground quickly, is good in the air and alert to danger.
Crucially, he also has three years' worth of top-flight experience in England behind him, having moved to Brighton from Lille when he was 19. It gives him the edge on Santos, also 22, and it will be interesting to see whether the pair compete for the same place at the base of Michael Carrick's midfield or if, against the best sides, they might play together.
It will also be fascinating to see if he gets asked to fill in at left-back too.
He has played there before and, unlike Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui - who could also switch sides if Luke Shaw is unavailable - is left-footed.
Paul Pogba is the only midfield player United have signed for more than the Â£70m they are committing to Baleba which, given his age, is a statement in itself.
'Baleba complements United's other midfielders'
![Carlos Baleba signs his Manchester United contract](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/819/cpsprodpb/b447/live/4f845f10-a0a1-11f1-84a9-276d1a8e5a22.jpg)
Brighton have inserted a sell-on clause for Baleba into the deal
Baleba's appeal lies less in creativity and more in his ability to win possession, cover ground and then carry his team forward.
His 2025-26 campaign was quieter than the previous one, but his 2024-25 numbers show why United have tracked him for so long. He ranked fourth among Premier League midfielders for possessions won in the middle third (107) and interceptions (46), was fifth for ball recoveries (197) and seventh for duels won (199).
That defensive output was matched by his ability to progress possession himself.
Baleba averaged 6.7 progressive carries per 90 minutes, with only three qualifying Premier League defensive midfielders recording more, while 2.9 of those carries travelled at least 10 metres.
His athleticism underpins that game as he reached a top speed of 34.5km/h in 2024-25, compared with 30.5km/h for Casemiro, and averaged 8.2 defensive actions per 90.
He is not necessarily the midfielder United would rely on to dictate possession. Only 11.8% of his passes were classed as line-breaking that season and 22.7% travelled forward - both below the average for central and defensive midfielders.
But that may make him complementary to United's other options rather than a direct alternative. Tielemans can provide more of the progressive distribution, while Baleba offers defensive security and the ability to drive through midfield.
Alongside Kobbie Mainoo, he could take on more of the ball-winning and ground-covering work, while a partnership with Santos could allow Baleba greater freedom to operate box to box.
That versatility is reflected in his positioning as he spent 88% of his minutes last season as a defensive midfielder and 12% in central midfield, suggesting he can anchor the side or step forward depending on who plays alongside him.
United most commonly defended in a 4-2-2-2 last season under Carrick, accounting for 55.9% of their out-of-possession shapes. Baleba's dynamism could be especially valuable in a system where central midfielders are asked to defend large spaces and stop counter-attacks.
There may, however, be an adaptation period.
Baleba is recovering from an ankle ligament injury suffered in pre-season and will need time to recover his match sharpness.
United have also looked to spend longer spells in possession under Carrick, progressing through midfield with quick combinations. Baleba's game is better suited to more open contests, but his passing profile suggests he may need time to adjust to greater responsibility in build-up.
His left foot and mobility should still make him a natural partner for players such as Tielemans or Bruno Fernandes. There is development ahead of him at 22, not least after last season's dip, but at his best Baleba combines defensive activity with the acceleration and carrying power to transform a turnover into an attack within seconds.
summary: Manchester United has signed Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a deal worth up to £70m. The 22-year-old has agreed to a five-year contract with an option for an additional year. Baleba arrives to add physicality, power, and defensive security to United's midfield, though he is currently recovering from an ankle injury.
key_points: Manchester United paid an initial £65m plus £5m in add-ons for Carlos Baleba.
Brighton negotiated a sell-on clause as part of the agreement.
Baleba signed a five-year contract with an option to extend for another year.
He brings strong defensive qualities, athleticism, and ball-winning ability to United's midfield.
Baleba is currently sidelined with an ankle injury sustained during Brighton's pre-season training.

title: Arsenal close to club-record sale before deadline after Arteta talks
author: Matt Verri
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Arsenal Football Newsletter](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_arsenal_embed_desktop.png)
There has been a growing sense that Martinelli's time at Arsenal is coming to an end after seven years in north London.
While Martinelli had initially been keen to stay at Arsenal, and turned down a move to Turkey amid interest from Galatasaray, honest discussions with manager Arteta over his position in the squad have left the Brazilian more open to leaving.
A final agreement has not yet been reached, with Arsenal valuing Martinelli at around £60million. Al-Hilal are hoping to strike a deal closer to £50m.
However, talks are advancing positively and Martinelli has been offered a contract that would involve a huge increase on his current £180,000-a-week salary.
If the deal goes through, as appears increasingly likely, it will represent Arsenal's record sale.
As it stands, the £35m received for selling Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to Liverpool in 2017 is the highest fee Arsenal have brought in for a departing player.
Martinelli has been at Arsenal for the entirety of Arteta's reign, signing from Brazilian side Ituano in the summer of 2019 for a fee of around £6m.
He has gone on to score 62 goals for the club and, after several near-misses in recent years, played his part in the title-winning campaign last season.
Martinelli's exit continues Arsenal's refreshing of their left wing. Leandro Trossard departed earlier this summer for Besiktas, with Christos Tzolis signed as a replacement from Club Brugge.
It is not certain that Martinelli will also be directly replaced in the final week of the transfer window.
Read More
Arsenal had long-term interest in Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz, but he has picked up a foot injury and faces a spell on the sidelines.
Julian Alvarez remains the top target, though that is a complicated deal to do and Arsenal are still waiting for encouragement from his representatives.
The Gunners are willing to be ambitious financially if Alvarez does become available to them, as they were with Vinicius Jr earlier this summer.
However, they will not spend big for the sake of it on players that are priced well beyond the club's own valuations.
summary: Arsenal are closing in on a club-record sale of Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal following honest discussions between the player and manager Mikel Arteta. Arsenal value the Brazilian winger at £60 million while Al-Hilal are aiming for a £50 million deal, though talks are advancing positively. If completed, the transfer will surpass Arsenal's previous record sale of £35 million for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017.
key_points: Martinelli is open to leaving Arsenal after seven years following discussions with Mikel Arteta.
Al-Hilal has offered Martinelli a contract with a massive increase on his current £180,000-a-week salary.
Arsenal value Martinelli at £60 million, while Al-Hilal is targeting a £50 million agreement.
The potential deal would surpass Arsenal's previous record sale of £35 million for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain.

title: Sir Billy Boston: 'A world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told'
author: Matt Newsum
content:
![Billy Boston in a black and white photo looks forward](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1440/cpsprodpb/4e34/live/bc31b550-a078-11f1-bf10-9547e884d7b7.jpg)
Billy Boston spent almost all of his decorated career at Wigan
- Published
When Sir Billy Boston was knighted in 2025, it was a unique moment for rugby league.
For the first time, this rebel sport from the north of England had been recognised in such a manner; one of its heroes had been acknowledged for their contribution to history through the game.
Sir Billy was a fitting recipient of the honour and a world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told.
You can tell the importance of someone by how many statutes have been erected in tribute, and Sir Billy Boston wasn't lacking.
His name was chosen as one of just five to grace Wembley's monument to rugby league's Challenge Cup, while years after his departure north, his home city of Cardiff also ensured his legacy remained cast-iron strong as he formed part of a three-man tribute along with Clive Sullivan and Gus Risman.
Unsurprisingly, Boston is also captured in bronze in his adopted home of Wigan; the place where his legend really came to life.
Born and brought up in Cardiff's ethnically-eclectic Tiger Bay district, he learned his rugby skills on the streets and with the talent factory-esque Cardiff International Athletic Club.
Like all Welsh lads he harboured dreams of playing for his local club Cardiff RFC and hopefully the national team.
Like others before and after for a time, Boston found those routes blocked, having to travel to Neath and Pontypridd to trial before his military service took him north.
It was here where the league scouts came calling, and Wigan persuaded Boston to turn professional in 1953, forever ending his union dreams in the time of 'sine die' penalties for liaising with league personnel.
The money was life changing.
Â£3,000 could easily buy a house at that stage, while it proved money well spent as he took to the new code like a duck to water, scoring with his first touch in a Wigan A team game.
This prime specimen of Welsh breezeblock had everything; he was quick, he could step and as former player and BBC commentator Ray French put it - his fend was like "being hit in the face with shovel".
The sepia footage and slow shutter speeds of the cameras that captured his magic during his playing days simply cannot dull his brilliance.
Whether it was bustling over for another try in cherry and white hoops at Wembley or crushing the Aussies at Sydney Cricket Ground, Boston was a blur of speed, footwork and power.
Having swiftly progressed to the first team at Central Park, he would go on to score 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan, and tales of his feats would be passed down through generations. There are very few down at the Brick Community Stadium these days who don't know of Sir Billy, young or old, his name carried a cache right until his last.
![Sir Billy Boston looks to his right with a big smile on his face](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/5756/live/2303c560-a07a-11f1-bfeb-dfb02ea642ef.jpg)
Sir Billy Boston attended last season's Grand Final between Hull KR and Wigan
Great Britain gave him the international recognition denied to him by Wales, and he rewarded the selectors by racking up the tries, particularly against the Australians who would bear the brunt of his scoring ability.
He scored 36 tries alone on his maiden Great Britain tour, dazzling both Australia and New Zealand in 1954 under captain and fellow Welshman Dickie Williams.
Boston was a phenomenal rugby league player, but there is also a powerful message in how in post-war Britain a black athlete could become a hugely popular figure by communities adjusting to a new, more diverse world.
Others like Roy Francis beforehand, Johnny Freeman, and Colin Dixon, also became established names, but never quite sprinkled the same stardust as Sir Billy.
It paved the way for players such as Ellery Hanley and Martin Offiah to charm the public with their talents, while modern day talent such as Junior Nsemba and Kai Pearce-Paul continues to stand out in a sport which has broken down barriers for years.
Sir Billy had a unique unifying effect on a normally partisan and tribal rugby league community.
He was revered naturally in Wigan, his adopted home, but you won't hear a boo or jeer at mention of Boston anywhere - not even at sworn rivals St Helens where they appreciate a good footballer when they see one.
Still a regular visitor to Wigan games right up to his passing, it was always a beautiful moment when the cameras found him, the crowd spotting him on the screen bursting into cheer, and the realisation creeping over his face in the shape of a smile.
There was a photo of him and his wife Lady Joan, who had died just a few weeks previously, on her seat with flowers at Wigan's game with Wakefield last week. There is a poignancy that Sir Billy departed soon after her.
His seat will always be reserved at Wigan, and he will be dearly missed but certainly not forgotten.
summary: Sir Billy Boston, who was knighted in 2025, was a legendary rugby league player celebrated for his remarkable athletic career, primarily with Wigan. Growing up in Cardiff's Tiger Bay, he turned professional with Wigan in 1953 after facing barriers in rugby union. He scored 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan and achieved international success with Great Britain, becoming a revered and unifying figure in the sport.
key_points: Sir Billy Boston received a knighthood in 2025, marking a historic recognition for rugby league.
He scored 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan after turning professional in 1953.
He faced blocked pathways in Welsh rugby union before moving north to excel in rugby league.
He achieved significant international success, scoring heavily for Great Britain against touring teams.
He was widely revered across the sport, transcending tribal rivalries and paving the way for future diverse athletes.

title: Joe Root: I am really hacked off at Brydon Carse
author: Will Macpherson
content:
![Joe Root looks furious](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/cricket/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499503429_17876627959820_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq-yKXUOr_MwQ_nCnkwkIf1F5NUcTKNHKqy85KLqtvPLE.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Joe Root looks furious](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/cricket/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499503429_17876627959820_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq-yKXUOr_MwQ_nCnkwkIf1F5NUcTKNHKqy85KLqtvPLE.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Joe Root said he is “really hacked off” to be discussing another “stupid mistake” by an England player after Brydon Carse’s nightclub scandal.
In an attempt to draw a line in the sand over his team’s behaviour after Carse was briefly detained by police last weekend, the England Test captain laid down the law to his players ahead of this week’s second Test against Pakistan.
Carse was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly, before being de-arrested soon after, in the early hours of Sunday morning while on a night out with Ben Stokes and other Durham team-mates in Derby.
The 31-year-old has been dropped from the England squad for Thursday’s second Test at Lord’s. He was an unused member of the squad who won at Headingley, and was sent instead to play for his county Durham. They beat Derbyshire on Saturday, after which the trouble began during celebrations.
It was the latest in a string of off-field incidents during the past year, starting with Harry Brook being punched by a nightclub bouncer in Wellington, hours before leading England in a one-day international. A boozy Ashes tour followed, then Stokes and Gus Atkinson stayed out beyond the team’s midnight curfew after the first Test win over New Zealand, an incident which ultimately led to Stokes’s international retirement in June.
Root brought forward his captain’s press conference by 24 hours in order to address the issue. He was unable to provide specific details because the matter is in the hands of the Cricket Regulator, which is investigating Carse’s behaviour. Derbyshire Police say they are not investigating the matter.
“If I’m being brutally honest I’m really hacked off,” Root said. “I’m really disappointed that, after last week’s performance, we’re sat here and we’re talking about something that is not related to it at all.
“In terms of the incident itself, it’s obviously with the regulator and there’s not a lot I can say about it. It’s in their hands now.
“I’ve spoken to Brydon – when I first found out my first concern was him as a person. He’s someone I’ve spent a lot of time with, who’s spent a lot of time in this dressing room, and you develop personal relationships with players.
“I don’t think I’m speaking out of turn in saying he’s very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I’m sure when he gets his chance he will say that himself.
“It’s not the isolated incident itself, it’s the fact we continuously keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it’s detracting from what we are doing on the field.”
![Brydon Carse is congratulated by Joe Root after taking the wicket of Cameron Green during day three of the Fifth Test in the 2025/26 Ashes Series between Australia and England at Sydney Cricket Ground on January 06, 2026](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/cricket/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499371140_17876681041120_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqedA4kygIe6vqv6EOMEWOUq4c4gCXrrZtMhZwdsz1dlo.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Root returned to the captaincy after Stokes’s retirement, and instantly ditched the curfew, which had been brought in after the Ashes. Root had called on his players to behave like “adults”, only for Carse to get in trouble with the police days later. Root drew a line in the sand on the team’s culture. He is due to be joined by a new head coach, Stephen Fleming, next month, and is determined to transform the side’s image into one in which the players are “exceptional off the field”.
Root added that he is “not trying to sit here and ask people to be saints”, but “robust conversations” with players about their behaviour had taken place.
“My concern is what happens moving from this point,” he said. “We have an opportunity now, to create something and build something, that around the cricket we can be really proud of. We made good strides on the field last week. From this moment forward, and for a long period. This is not something I want to forget about in a week’s time, or a few weeks’ time or six weeks’ time, this is something we want to live and breathe every day. That is my concern, that is my focus.
“Clearly we are not portraying ourselves how we want to and I think we have an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong, that we can be proud of, that is player-driven and of course that isn’t going to happen overnight.
“We have already had conversations as a team on what is expected from this group of players, what it means to play for England, what it takes to play for England. We want to create something that we can be proud of, that people who follow us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and not just revere what we do on the field but off it as well.
“Over the next little while as leader of this team, with Stephen and the group of players themselves, it’s to make something that is just that.
“It’s important we create something bigger, it’s about having something long lasting that we can be proud of, that we can pass on to the next generation of players for them to evolve and be proud of.
“I might only be in this dressing room for a couple more years, maybe a bit longer than that. There’s a group of players there that are going to be around for the next 10 years, and they can live and breathe something and achieve something over that period of time.”
Carse travelled to London with Stokes, who was doing commercial work, on Sunday, but has now left and will play for Durham on Thursday. Michael Vaughan, the former England captain, had called for a punishment that “sends a shiver down the whole England cricket team”.
England are yet to name a team for the second Test. Pakistan look likely to welcome back their captain Babar Azam after a hand injury.
summary: England Test captain Joe Root expressed deep frustration after Brydon Carse was briefly detained by police for being drunk and disorderly during a night out in Derby. Carse has been dropped from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's following this latest off-field incident. Root used the situation to lay down the law regarding team behavior and wants to build a culture that players can be proud of both on and off the field.
key_points: Brydon Carse was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and subsequently de-arrested in Derby.
Carse has been dropped from England's squad for the second Test against Pakistan and sent to play for Durham.
Joe Root brought forward his press conference to address the incident and expressed deep frustration over repeated off-field mistakes.
Root aims to establish a stronger, player-driven team culture alongside incoming head coach Stephen Fleming.

title: Brydon Carse: Joe Root says he is 'hacked off' and 'disappointed' at nightclub incident
author: Ffion Wynne
content:
![Joe Root speaks to the media with sponsors boards behind him](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/f63b/live/5cb95b00-a082-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Joe Root spoke to the media at Lord's on Tuesday afternoon, having had a "strong" conversation with the England players earlier in the day
- Published
England captain Joe Root says he is "hacked off" and "disappointed" at the incident involving fast bowler Brydon Carse at a Derby nightclub.
Carse, 31, was dropped from the squad for the second Test starting against Pakistan this week.
Images that appeared on social media on Sunday showed Carse, 31, in handcuffs outside a bar in Derby on Saturday night and he was briefly arrested and subsequently de-arrested.
"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off, I'm really disappointed," Root said in the opening to a news conference.
"After last week's performance, we're sat here and we're talking about something that is not related to it at all."
The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has referred the incident to the Cricket Regulator and Carse was replaced in the squad by Sonny Baker, with the Test starting at Lord's on Thursday.
Carse was not on England duty at the time of the incident as he was released to play for Durham, but he is a centrally contracted player.
Root also said he had spoken to his England team-mate about the incident, and expressed his frustration at the "stupid mistakes" that are continually being made.
"I've spoken to Brydon, and when I first found out my main concern was him as a person," Root added.
"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn by saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure that when he gets his chance he will say that himself.
"But I don't think it's the isolated incident itself, it's the fact we keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."
In October, England white-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer outside a nightclub in Wellington, New Zealand, with team-mates Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue also present.
During the Ashes tour of Australia, opener Ben Duckett was filmed apparently drunk on England's holiday in Noosa.
And in June, former Test captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson broke a team curfew and were present when a member of England's security staff was punched by a Saracens rugby player in a London nightclub.
In this latest incident, Carse was with Durham team-mates Stokes and Matthew Potts, all of whom are under England central contracts. In Stokes' case, the England deal remains in place despite his international retirement in June.
It makes a total of eight contracted players who have been involved in or present for late-night incidents in the past year â more than a quarter of the 30 men on England deals.
When he was reappointed as Test captain, Root confirmed he would remove the midnight curfew which was previously in place during Stokes and Brendon McCullum's regime after a string of off-field incidents during the Ashes over the winter.
Root stood by that decision, saying he still did not think it was "the right way to go", but admitted it would take some time for the team to be trusted by the fans again.
"In many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back, and it's something that we're going to have to live and breathe consistently," he said.
"I might only be in this dressing room for a couple more years, but there is a group of players there who might be in there for another 10.
"I've made it very clear how we want to conduct ourselves, and now we've got to live it and show people what I see day in, day out in the dressing room, which is a group of characters who know what it means to play for England and not having incidents define how we are seen as players. That's going to take some work and time."
Root also confirmed he had spoken to his predecessor Stokes, who was also seen in the social media video, but only to check in on Carse's wellbeing.
He was asked what potential consequences Carse might face but said he would have no involvement as it is in the hands of the regulator, and was keen to reiterate that he was focusing on moving forward and "building something to be proud of".
"I don't think the recent past has been a good look," Root, 35, said.
"It's our responsibility to change that. I see the dressing room every day and how we operate around cricket and it's very impressive.
"But at the same time, I can understand why we are viewed in a certain way and in a certain light at the moment.
"That's what lies ahead of us, to change that. I just think, if we don't put ourselves in certain situations, it's not something we will have to worry about."
summary: England captain Joe Root expressed deep disappointment and frustration after fast bowler Brydon Carse was briefly arrested outside a Derby nightclub. Carse was dropped from the squad for the upcoming second Test against Pakistan and the ECB referred the incident to the Cricket Regulator. Root emphasized that the team must work to regain the trust of fans following a series of recurring off-field night-out incidents involving centrally contracted players.
key_points: Brydon Carse was dropped from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan after being briefly arrested outside a Derby nightclub.
Joe Root stated he is 'hacked off' and disappointed by the repeated off-field mistakes made by players away from the game.
The ECB has referred Carse's incident to the Cricket Regulator, and Sonny Baker replaced him in the squad.
Root noted that eight centrally contracted players have been involved in or present for late-night incidents over the past year.

title: FPL notes: Palmer + Palestra injury latest, Alonso on Chelsea attack
author: FPLReactions
content:
Chelsea edged Fulham 3-2 in Xabi Alonso’s first competitive match in charge.
Cole Palmer (£9.5m) starred, Morgan Rogers (£7.5m) impressed on his Premier League debut for Chelsea and Joao Pedro (£7.5m) continued his excellent pre-season form.
Here are our Scout Notes from Craven Cottage.
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Screen-Shot-2026-08-25-at-09.42.37-914x1024.jpg)
PALMER STARS + ROGERS CREATES FIVE
![Palmer haul](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-24T201432Z_1769515919_UP1EM8O1K87RG_RTRMADP_3_SOCCER-ENGLAND-FUL-CHE-1-1024x700.jpg)
Chelsea’s front three all delivered attacking returns.
Palmer led the way with a goal and assist, continuing to occupy one of the two attacking roles behind Joao Pedro.
His first return arrived after only 32 seconds. Palmer’s clever flick released Joao Pedro behind the Fulham defence, with the Brazilian lifting his finish over Bernd Leno (£4.5m).
Palmer then got on the scoresheet shortly after half-time. Joao Pedro carried possession forward before releasing his team-mate, who finished through Leno’s legs.
The underlying numbers backed up an impressive display. Palmer created three chances and registered two shots on target.
Alonso was particularly pleased with the freedom and responsibility Palmer showed:
“I’m very happy for Cole, because I have really enjoyed seeing him playing with this dynamism, with this freedom, with this responsibility, helping the team, feeling important and we need that for the team. If Cole feels this way, we will have a better team, a better Chelsea.” – Xabi Alonso on Cole Palmer
There was a slight concern late on, with Palmer asking to come off before Geovany Quenda (£5.5m) replaced him in the 82nd minute.
Nothing alarming emerged from Alonso’s post-match press conference, however. The Chelsea boss spoke glowingly about Palmer’s performance and did not flag an injury when discussing him.
So, unless further information emerges before Gameweek 2, there is no confirmed injury at this stage.
Palmer wasn’t Chelsea’s most creative player on Monday, however.
That accolade went to Rogers, who created a match-high five chances and also scored on his Premier League debut for the club.
![Palmer haul](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-2026-08-25T062452.640-1024x393.jpg)
Above: Chelsea players sorted by chances created (CC) v Fulham
Rogers swept home Maxence Lacroix’s (£6.0m) low cross shortly before half-time, having already threatened with a powerful blocked effort.
His combination of creativity and goal threat would have appealed to both fans and FPL managers.
“They are going to be a very important part of the team. To build around them, no. To build the team with them. They need to take responsibility, they need to lead the rest, they need to inspire the rest.” – Xabi Alonso on Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro
PEDRO FORM CONTINUES
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-24T194109Z_1814443581_UP1EM8O1IOKQP_RTRMADP_3_SOCCER-ENGLAND-FUL-CHE-1-1024x716.jpg)
Joao Pedro carried his excellent pre-season form straight into Gameweek 1.
Chelsea’s central striker needed just 32 seconds to score, racing clear before producing a composed finish over Leno.
He then supplied Palmer’s goal, carrying the ball into the Fulham half before timing his pass into the midfielder’s path.
The Brazilian created two chances and registered four shots.
![Palmer haul](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-2026-08-25T062906.589.jpg)
Above: Joao Pedro’s shot map v Fulham
There were further openings, too.
Joao Pedro volleyed a Palmer cross narrowly wide in the first half and later fired over from distance. He even had the ball in the net again late on after reacting first to Quenda’s saved effort, only for an offside in the build-up to rule it out.
His minutes were arguably just as encouraging.
While Palmer and Rogers departed late on, Joao Pedro completed the full 90 minutes as Chelsea’s central striker.
After his prolific pre-season, another goal and assist only strengthen his position as one of the more interesting Chelsea attackers heading into the upcoming schedule.
NO CAICEDO OR PALESTRA, JAMES IN MIDFIELD
Two notable absences forced Alonso to alter his expected line-up.
Moises Caicedo (£5.5m) and Marco Palestra (£5.5m) both missed the matchday squad after suffering minor setbacks during the week.
“They had minor setbacks during the week, so they were not fit to play tonight.” – Xabi Alonso on Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra
Alonso later confirmed that Caicedo’s issue had developed during the week but offered no suggestion of a lengthy absence.
In Palestra’s absence, Malo Gusto (£5.0m) started at right wing-back, with Jorrel Hato (£4.5m) on the opposite flank.
Reece James (£5.5m) again operated centrally in midfield, this time alongside Romeo Lavia (£5.0m).
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-2026-08-25T063345.975.jpg)
Above: Reece James’s heatmap v Fulham
Chelsea retained the back-three structure Alonso repeatedly used late in pre-season. Josh Acheampong (£4.5m), Lacroix and Levi Colwill (£5.0m) formed the defensive trio.
Lavia completed 65 minutes before Enzo Fernandez (£7.0m) replaced him.
Alonso explained that the decision to start Lavia ahead of Fernandez reflected the different stages of preparation within his squad.
“We have different options, players that during the pre-season they come in different stages, so all the players will play an important role. This is about the team, this is about the squad.” – Xabi Alonso
Fernandez subsequently played fewer than 30 minutes, while new signing Pep Chavarria (£5.0m) made his league debut after replacing Hato.
Pedro Neto (£6.5m), Estevao (£6.5m) and Quenda also appeared from the bench.
There are therefore still several selection questions to answer once Palestra and Caicedo return.
LACROIX DEFCON, SANCHEZ ERRORS
Lacroix enjoyed an eventful league debut for Chelsea.
The centre-back supplied the assist for Rogers’ goal, collecting Palmer’s pass before beating his man and driving a low ball across the six-yard box.
He also reached the defensive contribution (DefCon) threshold:
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-2026-08-25T063727.533.jpg)
Chelsea still conceded twice, however.
Josh King (£5.5m) first forced Robert Sanchez (£5.0m) into a reaction save before beating him at the near post for Fulham’s equaliser.
The hosts struck again shortly after Palmer made it 3-1. Timothy Castagne (£4.5m) forced another Sanchez stop and Gonzalo Garcia (£6.0m) reacted quickest to the rebound.
Fulham finished with 14 attempts and two big chances, while Sanchez also had to deny substitute Ryan Sessegnon (£4.5m) late on.
Antonee Robinson (£4.5m) sent another presentable opportunity narrowly wide.
Sanchez’s display will inevitably attract scrutiny, particularly with Mike Penders (£4.5m) waiting in the squad.
Alonso refused to pin the goals on his goalkeeper, though.
“It’s about the team, it’s not about the individual. The first goal, we can do better to defend, we can do better to avoid, but it’s part of the game. All the lines, from the strikers, the midfielders, the defence, the goalkeepers, we want to do better in everything.” – Xabi Alonso
KING + GARCIA ON TARGET
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-24T201850Z_1877274330_UP1EM8O1KFDRS_RTRMADP_3_SOCCER-ENGLAND-FUL-CHE-1-1024x727.jpg)
There was plenty to interest FPL managers on the Fulham side, too.
Josh King completed the full 90 minutes and scored, having already forced Sanchez into a save before his equaliser.
His manager was particularly enthusiastic afterwards.
“I have been talking during all the summer with Josh King; what a player we have here, amazing! What a player, unbelievable. They need to make numbers… they need to score goals because, at the end, it’s the most important thing in football. And I hope they can score many goals this season.” – Alvaro Arbeloa
Garcia’s involvement was another significant selection clue.
The summer signing led the line, completed the full 90 minutes and scored Fulham’s second goal.
Rodrigo Muniz (£5.5m), by contrast, did not enter until the 82nd minute.
It is only one match, but Garcia starting and completing the game provides an encouraging early indication of his minutes under Arbeloa.
Cesar Palacios (£5.5m) also made his Premier League debut, while Oscar Bobb (£5.5m) started in the attacking line behind Garcia.
At the back, Jorge Cuenca (£4.5m) was Fulham’s only defender to reach the DefCon threshold.
Castagne at least added attacking involvement, with his saved effort leading directly to Garcia’s goal.
Fulham ultimately left empty-handed but caused Chelsea plenty of problems with their high press and aggressive approach.
“I think we showed the character and personality that I want my players to show. We did what we have to do: press, play with character, try to play in their half like we did, and try to create chances to score goals, and to be ambitious.” – Alvaro Arbeloa
For FPL managers, King’s £5.5m price, goal and 90-minute outing immediately catch the eye.
Garcia’s start may be even more significant for the longer term, while Chelsea leave Craven Cottage with plenty of attacking encouragement but a few defensive and selection questions still to answer.
![New FPL Stats Centre: Find the best picks, differentials + DefCon stars 2](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-2026-08-19T080449.761-819x1024.jpg)
summary: Chelsea defeated Fulham 3-2 in Xabi Alonso's first competitive match in charge, driven by standout attacking performances from Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, and Joao Pedro. Both Palmer and Rogers found the net alongside Joao Pedro, who carried his strong pre-season form into Gameweek 1 with a goal and an assist. Meanwhile, Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra missed out due to minor weekly setbacks, and Fulham's Josh King and Gonzalo Garcia both got on the scoresheet for their side.
key_points: Cole Palmer registered a goal and an assist, though he asked to come off late with a minor concern that Alonso did not flag as an injury.
Morgan Rogers shone on his Premier League debut, creating a match-high five chances and scoring Chelsea's second goal.
Joao Pedro played the full 90 minutes as the central striker, contributing a goal, an assist, and four shots.
Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra missed the matchday squad after suffering minor setbacks during the week.
Josh King and summer signing Gonzalo Garcia both scored for Fulham, with Garcia leading the line and playing the full 90 minutes.

title: Savinho: Tottenham sign winger from Manchester City for Â£75m
author: Paul Battison; Mohamed Moallim
content:
![Savinho in action for Manchester City](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/f37b/live/af288520-a067-11f1-ab4b-e3f95ee34b2e.jpg)
Savinho has won 13 caps for Brazil, scoring one goal
- Published
Tottenham have signed Brazil winger Savinho from Manchester City for an initial Â£75m.
The 22-year-old has joined Spurs on a long-term contract with Roberto de Zerbi's side potentially paying a further Â£10m in add-ons.
Savinho's move to north London has been more than 12 months in the making, with Spurs failing in a bid to sign him last summer.
Savinho opted to remain at Etihad Stadium, but his game time was limited under Pep Guardiola last term when he made just seven Premier League starts.
"It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here," said Savinho.
"It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.
"As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team."
Savinho joined City from French side Troyes in a Â£30.8m deal in 2024 and has made 84 appearances for the club in total, scoring seven goals and providing 16 assists.
The Brazil international joins Spurs following the arrivals of Mateus Fernandes from West Ham, Sandro Tonali from Newcastle and Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton this summer for a combined Â£312m.
Spurs have also brought in defenders Marcos Senesi and Andrew Robertson in on free transfers and goalkeeper Martin Dubravka.
"Savio is a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity," said De Zerbi.
City also remain in advanced talks to sell Egypt forward Omar Marmoush to Spurs, and sources with knowledge of the situation say there is a "good chance" the deal gets completed before the 1 September transfer deadline.
Savinho brings a different route forward
Savinho's involvement for City fell sharply last season after the club signed winger Antoine Semenyo from Bournemouth in January.
He played 821 Premier League minutes, scoring once and providing one assist, while featuring in only 31% of City's available minutes across all competitions.
That was a significant drop from the previous campaign, when he played 54% of City's minutes.
Yet his 2024-25 numbers show why Tottenham are prepared to invest heavily in him. Savinho registered eight Premier League assists that season, all from open play, despite playing only 1,773 minutes. Only five players recorded more from open play.
On a per-90 basis, he ranked third for open-play assists with 0.41, while only Mohamed Salah created more chances per 90 than Savinho's 2.2.
His biggest threat, though, came from carrying the ball. Among Premier League players with at least 1,000 minutes in 2024-25, only Jeremy Doku averaged more progressive carries of at least 10 metres than Savinho's 6.8 per 90.
Savinho also led the division for carries followed by a chance created, averaging 1.3 per 90, while only Son Heung-min ended a carry with an assist more frequently.
He completed 2.6 dribbles per 90 with a 51% success rate and used those carries to draw defenders towards him before releasing team-mates.
That ability was even more evident during his breakout season at Girona. Savinho played 2,989 minutes in La Liga in 2023-24, with 65% of them coming on the left wing. He scored nine goals, supplied eight assists and established himself as one of the division's most dangerous one-against-one players.
At City his role shifted. Across his two Premier League seasons, his most common position was on the right, accounting for 36% of his minutes, compared with 20% on the left. That versatility could matter at Spurs.
summary: Tottenham Hotspur has signed Brazil winger Savinho from Manchester City for an initial £75m on a long-term contract, with potential add-ons of £10m. The 22-year-old experienced limited playing time under Pep Guardiola last season following the arrival of Antoine Semenyo. Savinho joins a busy summer transfer window for Spurs under manager Roberto de Zerbi.
key_points: Savinho signed for Tottenham from Manchester City for an initial £75m, plus a potential £10m in add-ons.
He has earned 13 caps for the Brazil national team and previously played for French side Troyes and Girona.
His playing time at Manchester City decreased last season after the January arrival of Antoine Semenyo.
During the 2024-25 season, Savinho excelled in progressive ball-carrying and creating chances from open play.
Tottenham's summer additions also include Mateus Fernandes, Sandro Tonali, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Andrew Robertson, and Martin Dubravka.

Manchester City have entered the race to sign Liverpool and Netherlands forward Cody Gakpo, 27, with Tottenham also still working on a deal. (Soccer News NL - Dutch)
Sticking with Liverpool, it seems there could be more business to be done, both in terms of incomings and outgoings, before next week's transfer deadline.
Reports in the Netherlands last night claimed Manchester City had made contact with the representatives of Cody Gakpo, who is also attracting interest from Tottenham.
