Liverpool right-back Calvin Ramsay has joined Scottish side St Mirren on a season-long loan.
The 23-year-old, capped once by Scotland, joined the Reds in 2022 from Aberdeen on a five-year deal.
Ramsay has made four senior appearance for Liverpool but is yet to feature in the Premier League.
His departure frees up a spot for a non-homegrown player to arrive at Merseyside.
Clubs can register a maximum of 17 players not classed as a 'homegrown player'.
A homegrown player is a player who, regardless of their nationality or age, has been affiliated with any English or Welsh club for a period of three entire seasons or 36 months before their 21st birthday.
Earlier this month, Ronald Araujo's arrival took Liverpool's non-homegrown player quota to 17, which hit the limit.
We have some transfer news to bring you from Anfield.
Liverpool have sanctioned the departure of a defender, and it could have significant implications for their Premier League squad quota...
Can you remember the last time an Aston Villa forward pushed for a move to the Saudi Pro League? That's right, it was Jhon Duran in January 2025.
Since then, the Colombian forward - who was one of the most exciting young strikers in Europe at the time - has been loaned out to three different clubs after failing to impress at Al-Nassr.
Could Ollie Watkins learn from Duran's downfall that the grass isn't always greener after leaving Villa Park?
Here are Aston Villa's incomings this summer:
Alejandro Garnacho [Chelsea - Aston Villa] Loan
Aaron Wan-Bissaka [West Ham - Aston Villa] Loan
Modou Keba Cisse [LASK - Aston Villa] Â£4.2m
Matteo Ruggeri [Atletico Madrid - Aston Villa] Â£17m
Zion Suzuki [Parma - Aston Villa] in the region of Â£30m
Joao Gomes [Wolves - Aston Villa] Â£38m
Johan Manzambi [Freiburg - Aston Villa] Over Â£50m
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery said Ollie Watkins' absence in the 4-0 thrashing at Brighton is a "question for him".
The 30-year-old was left out of the matchday squad for Villa's Premier League opener after Emery confirmed earlier in the week there had been offers from Saudi club Al-Hilal for the striker.
Asked if it was his decision to leave Watkins out, Emery told Match of the Day: "This question is for him. You can call him and try to get his answer.
"The players here wanted to play and we had two strikers with a small injury. The question on Watkins is for him."
Watkins could become the latest of Villa's European heroes to exit this summer.
Villa ended a 30-year wait for a trophy by lifting the Europa League in May against Freiburg.
But the club could have sold six of the starting XI by the end of the transfer window.
"We are building the team. Last year and two years ago we were building the team in August," said Emery after the defeat at Brighton.
Sad to see Villa and Newcastle, two clubs being run so well, constrained by PSR. Arsenal have shown how sustained squad investment over several years can build a genuine contender. If others canât do the same, maybe the rules need a rethink.
Jasper, Leeds
Villa and Newcastle being forced to sell their best players, meanwhile Chelsea are selling players to themselves and no one bats an eyelid. Modern football is rotten.
Steve, Leeds
Here are Aston Villa's outgoings this summer:
Morgan Rogers [Aston Villa - Chelsea] Â£117m
Ezri Konsa [Aston Villa - Arsenal] Â£55m
Youri Tielemans [Aston Villa - Manchester United] Â£35m
Donyell Malen [Aston Villa - Roma] Undisclosed fee
Enzo Barreneche [Aston Villa - Valencia] Loan
Lewis Dobbin [Aston Villa - Southampton] Â£9m
Lucas Digne [Aston Villa - PSG] Â£8.5m
![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/128/cpsprodpb//vivo/live/images/2026/2/9/9e5c089b-2e9b-4602-b743-ff14a7b27fe0.jpg.webp) Nick Mashiter
BBC Sport football news reporter
Like many, Aston Villa are a selling club, mainly down to necessity, and have been for a number of years.
They must comply with Uefa's squad cost ratio (SCR) which restricts them to spending 70% of their football related revenue on player and staff wages, transfer fees and agent fees.
They have already been fined twice by Uefa for breaches, being hit with a Â£9.5m sanction last year and a Â£19.4m fine in June, although Â£12.9m was suspended after Villa came to a settlement agreement with Europe's governing body. But it has meant the club's hands are tied in the transfer window.
The Premier League's Profit and Sustainability Rules (PSR) also limited financial losses to a maximum of Â£105m over a rolling three-year period.
In their latest accounts, ending 30 June 2025, Villa had a post-tax profit of Â£17m but their two previous years showed losses of Â£119.6m (2023) and Â£85.4m (2024).
The regulations have now been replaced by SCR, meaning the Premier League falls in line with Uefa's model.
"It's necessity because of the rules," one former Villa executive told BBC Sport, when asked about the sales. "The PSR, the SCR, issues are well documented.
"It does seem slightly unfair they're having their ambition capped at this level. But it has forced this very big churn of players, which is unfortunate.
"Some will be forced due to PSR, some will be player demand. Combined it makes a big problem for Emery and certainly it is a lot to swallow in one go and to try and replace."
This summer has crystalised their situation because of the high-profile nature of the departures.
Villa had raised just over Â£200m with the sales of Jhon Duran (Â£71m), Douglas Luiz (Â£42.5m), Jacob Ramsey (Â£40m) and Moussa Diaby (Â£50m) over the past two years.
With the Ezri Konsa deal done, they have banked around Â£212m during this window, including Â£9m for Lewis Dobbin who never played a senior game for Villa before leaving for Southampton.
The academy has also paid its way comfortably with Jaden Philogene and Cameron Archer being bought back to be sold again, while Burnley spent Â£12m on Aaron Ramsey in 2023.
Internally, when Villa first returned to the Champions League in 2024, it was recognised it would be harder for academy prospects to break into the squad which left Villa more open to selling them.
Ollie Watkins has been brilliant for Villa But canât help think the decision to down tools is agent-led rather than player led. Emery deserves more respect though.
Alex, Stamford
I think Watkins has handled this badly to be honest, tarnishing his reputation as a Villa legend if he leaves like this.
Toby, Welwyn
If, as Emery hinted, Watkins refused to play- that is very poor from the player. He owes Villa more than that. There is however something very strange going on at Villa with such an exodus after a great season.
Robert, Belfast
![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/128/cpsprodpb//vivo/live/images/2024/7/1/ac19b0fc-d8e9-4783-9881-4b00877f7064.jpg.webp) Nizaar Kinsella
BBC Sport Chelsea reporter
Omari Kellyman remains highly regarded at Stamford Bridge, but a transfer that includes a buy-back clause is being viewed as a way to aid his development after an injury-hit period following his Â£19m move from Aston Villa in 2024.
The 20-year-old completed last season on loan at Cardiff City without injury, but his minutes had to be carefully managed after a series of hamstring problems since leaving Villa Park.
Strasbourg, also owned by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital through parent company BlueCo, are seen as a club where Kellyman can take the next step in his development after a series of setbacks.
It's the latest of more than a dozen moves between the clubs since BlueCo bought Strasbourg in 2023, a year after acquiring Chelsea.
Omari Kellyman has left Chelsea to join French side Strasbourg on a permanent deal.
The 20-year-old attacking midfielder failed to make a Premier League appearance for the Blues after joining from Aston Villa in June 2024.
However, Chelsea have inserted a buy-back clause in the deal with the French side.
Let's take a look at some of Ollie Watkins' Premier League stats since he joined Villa in September 2020:
2020/2021 - 14 goals, five assists
2021/2022 - 11 goals, two assists
2022/2023 - 15 goals, six assists
2023/2024 - 19 goals, 15 assists
2024/2025 - 16 goals, eight assists
2025/2026 - 16 goals, three assists
Al-Hilal, who have offered close to Â£40m, are not near to Aston Villa's asking price for Ollie Watkins. As next Tuesday's transfer deadline nears, Villa will play hardball for their all-time record Premier League goalscorer.
A deal is still believed to be some way off, even if Villa head coack Unai Emery revealed last week the striker could leave.
Al-Hilal, who signed Crysensio Summerville from West Ham in July, are likely to need to move one of their overseas players to make room for Watkins, despite loaning Darwin Nunez to Diriyah last week, so there are other moving parts in the deal.
Watkins has been training on his own, having returned from an extended break following the World Cup and is understood to have made his feelings clear to the Villa hierarchy about moving.
There have been no public comments from Watkins or his representatives but he is understood to be open to the move.
They have also kept quiet about Emery's response - particularly his enigmatic "silence" answer to Sky Sports' question on why his striker was not involved at Brighton, which appeared to lay the blame at Watkins' door.

title: Arsenal squad 'unhappy' with Mikel Arteta as Gabriel Martinelli nears £40m Al-Hilal transfer | Goal.com

content:

- Arsenal winger nears Emirates exitMartinelli is edging closer to a permanent Arsenal departure after manager Arteta explicitly instructed the Brazilian to find a new club. The talented winger is set to join Saudi Pro League outfit Al Hilal, bringing a sudden end to his hugely successful spell in north London. Despite being Arsenal's longest-serving player, the attacker has been entirely frozen out of recent matchday squads by the coaching staff. His impending exit marks a significant and ruthless shift for the Gunners, as Arteta takes aggressive steps to strengthen the squad that has just won the Premier League title.
- ![Arsenal FC v Real Betis Balompie - Pre-Season Friendly](https://assets.goal.com/images/v3/getty-2289363675/crop/MM5DCNJQGQ5DQNBWHJXG653FHIZTEMJ2GIYTK===/GettyImages-2289363675.jpg?auto=webp&format=pjpg&width=3840&quality=60) Getty Images Sport Squad frustrated over Martinelli treatmentArteta's harsh handling of the situation has seemingly not gone down well in the Emirates dressing room. According to ESPN, the manager's cut-throat approach has caused "some discomfort" among the Arsenal squad, with several team-mates feeling highly sympathetic towards the departing winger. The underlying tension escalated rapidly when Martinelli was excluded from the Community Shield victory over Manchester City, meaning he did not receive a winners' medal. The same report claims that this specific decision left the forward "greatly disappointed", while other senior squad members were also deeply unhappy with his outright omission.
- Signings signal the end for MartinelliThe writing appeared to be firmly on the wall earlier this summer when Arsenal completed a substantial £34 million deal for promising attacker Christos Tzolis. Furthermore, an audacious, albeit unsuccessful, pursuit of Real Madrid icon Vinicius Junior heavily suggested that Arteta was actively planning to revamp his left flank. Having made his initial first-team debut back in 2019, Martinelli has racked up nearly 300 appearances across all competitions for the club. Although his individual influence faded slightly last season, he still played a vital role in Arsenal's historic run to the Champions League final and their first top-flight crown since 2004.

While an approach from Turkish giants Galatasaray failed to excite him, Globo Esporte reports that he has officially given the green light to a lucrative Saudi Arabia switch despite some initial reluctance. The final transfer fee currently remains a point of negotiation between the respective clubs. Arsenal reportedly want a package of around £60m for their long-serving forward, but ESPN suggests the final agreed figure could be no more than £40m.

title: Liverpool’s midfield made Sunday League-level mistakes and Iraola must act now
author: Dominic King
content:
![Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499373715_17875677117380_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqa5yauG99kZAjRCW0LFy6f5gcpag9DDpntenR6QTnPnQ.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499373715_17875677117380_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqa5yauG99kZAjRCW0LFy6f5gcpag9DDpntenR6QTnPnQ.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
The most damaging criticism in football comes when you compare the Premier League with Sunday League.
You don’t expect those at the highest level to make the mistakes you would associate with those who trundle about on a weekend. But Liverpool left their disparagers with nowhere to go, other than the most rudimentary level, following a skittish afternoon on Tyneside.
It was obvious in real time that Liverpool had conceded bad goals in their 2-2 draw with Newcastle – Andoni Iraola’s frustration as he thundered on his way back to his seat after Joe Willock’s second was plain to see – but watching replays made for alarming viewing. Not everyone can run forward. Someone must stay back.
How Liverpool conceded less than 20 seconds after they should have had the game’s first shot was one thing; another entirely was how Yoane Wissa and Willock outfoxed six (yes, six) red shirts on their own to combine and re-establish Newcastle’s lead after Cody Gakpo had secured parity.
“The team has needed a defensive midfielder for three years,” said Daniel Sturridge, the former Liverpool striker, as he analysed the failings on Sky Sports. “If you analyse the midfield, they are all naturally attacking players… if I’m honest, Dominik Szoboszlai is better as a No 10.”
It’s not that he’s better, it’s where Szoboszlai, scorer of the game-saving penalty, feels most at home. When he was coming through the ranks at RB Salzburg then RB Leipzig – and with Hungary – he caught the eye in positions further up the pitch and his natural inclination is to go forward.
Szoboszlai was not to blame for Liverpool going behind after five minutes, not in a million years, but if you pause the screen when his partner Ryan Gravenberch elects to play a square ball, rather than shoot when he had the goal to aim at, the Hungarian is in a spot on the right that was once Mohamed Salah’s.
The still image is remarkable. If you look at it through optimistic eyes, you would say it shows Liverpool’s sense of adventure and commitment to attack, but the reality is they were as open as a building without any doors.
Amar Dedic’s sliding intervention should not have unlocked Liverpool, but it was essentially a straight ball through the middle, one that allowed William Osula and then Anthony Elanga to streak away. Osula was in an area of the pitch where you would have expected to see what is commonly called now a “No 6”.
“It’s absolutely normal in any type of profession that if you come in new and you have new plans and ideas that it takes a bit of time,” Virgil van Dijk said. “It is down to us to do it as soon as we can. We want to improve. We want to win. We want to do better. That’s what we are going to try and do.”
But was it a concern that the goals Liverpool conceded were so similar?
“I don’t think it is a worry,” Van Dijk said. “It is something we definitely have to improve – but it is not a worry. That’s the only thing I can say about it.”
Others, by contrast, will have plenty to say. The discussions will continue all through this week – that’s what happens when an issue looks so obvious – and part of the conversation will be fuelled by questions about what those in charge of the team can see that those in the stands can’t.
Liverpool have held a consistent line all summer. Whenever they have been asked about signing midfielders – and there have been many names, from Eduardo Camavinga to Tyler Adams to Lamine Camara – the answer has been the same: midfield is not an area in which they are recruiting.
The priority has been to get in a right-sided forward – a saga which appears to be drawing to a close if the noises around Yankuba Minteh are correct – and Bradley Barcola, even though negotiations with Paris St-Germain have been slow.
Exciting it all may seem, but when the consensus among those watching or attending is that they want someone to put their foot in and do the dirty work, they can’t all be wrong, and the way the contest materialised against Newcastle will have done nothing to assuage fears.
Since March 1, this group of Liverpool players has contested 17 matches in all competitions and kept only one clean sheet (against Fulham on April 11), and it is fanciful to believe they will make progress if they continue to be so porous.
“It is so early in the season that if we start panicking regardless of what could have happened (against Newcastle) then we won’t be in a good place,” Van Dijk concluded. “It is down to us to make sure we improve quickly, and that is what we try to do on the training ground.
“There were some good things, but also things that we have to improve.”
One area specifically. Van Dijk can see it, as it is directly in front of him. Everyone else can see it too, including Iraola, who was aghast at the way Newcastle were able to get through so easily. If he doesn’t sort out the middle, Liverpool are going to be in a muddle.
summary: Liverpool drew 2-2 with Newcastle after displaying major defensive vulnerabilities and midfield mistakes. Pundits and analysts highlighted the lack of a natural defensive midfielder as a primary issue for the squad. Despite these concerns, captain Virgil van Dijk urged calm and stated the team must improve quickly on the training ground.
key_points: Liverpool conceded two poor goals during their draw with Newcastle, exposing a lack of defensive stability.
Pundit Daniel Sturridge and other observers noted that Liverpool's midfield consists primarily of naturally attacking players rather than a traditional defensive No 6.
Liverpool have kept only one clean sheet in their last 17 matches across all competitions since March 1.
Club management has reportedly maintained all summer that midfield is not an area requiring recruitment, prioritizing forwards instead.

title: Gabriel Martinelli transfer news: Al Hilal and Arsenal make progress on deal for Brazilian winger
author: Luca Bendoni; Lyall Thomas
content:
Gabriel Martinelli transfer news: Al Hilal and Arsenal make progress on deal for Brazilian winger
Arsenal and Brazil winger Gabriel Martinelli is open to joining Al Hilal; the 25-year-old turned down an approach from Turkish side Galatasaray last week; Martinelli has been at Arsenal since 2019 and won the Premier League with the Gunners last season
Tuesday 25 August 2026 08:18, UK
Arsenal and Al Hilal have made progress in the last few days over a deal for Gabriel Martinelli.
Martinelli is seriously considering joining Al Hilal if a deal can be agreed between the clubs.
As an agreement on the fee nears, there is also expected to be a sell-on clause involved to the tune of 20 per cent of any future profit.

Arsenal are looking at potential new forward options themselves before the deadline, with Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez still their top target.
Reports have linked them with Juventus forward Kenan Yildiz, but he has picked up a left foot injury and could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines, according to Sky in Italy.
Sky in Italy are reporting that Juventus' medical staff are looking at various methods to find the best possible solution - but are not ruling out surgery that could rule him out for several weeks.
Martinelli was not named in the Arsenal matchday squad for the Community Shield win over Manchester City or the opening day victory over Coventry.
Analysis: Are Arsenal risking being short at left wing?
Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:
Arsenal started last season with Leandro Trossard and Martinelli as their two main left wing options. Should Martinelli's move to Al Hilal go through, they will start this season with neither of them.
Mikel Arteta's side are undergoing a slight revolution in that left-wing role, with Christos Tzolis set to be the only recognised left winger in the Arsenal squad.
The Greek winger has started his career in north London on fire - but with a week of the window to go, Arsenal could risk leaving themselves short on that flank.
Eberechi Eze came on as a left winger in Friday's win over Coventry, so there is cover in a makeshift area. The same applies to Noni Madueke, who has also featured on the left for Arsenal.
But Madueke and Eze both have an important role in providing cover and competition for Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard - who both don't have the best injury record. They may be needed elsewhere.
Arsenal's attacking targets are also slimming down. There is still interest in Atletico Madrid's Alvarez but that is far from a guarantee, with the Argentine's heart set on a move to Barcelona.
With Juventus' Yildiz now injured, sporting director Andrea Berta may have to produce a major move in the last week of the window.
Martinelli, meanwhile, departs Arsenal as a cult hero. He is one of three Arsenal players - alongside Saka and Reiss Nelson - who was in the Gunners squad when Arteta first took charge in December 2019.
He remained a popular player despite only scoring one Premier League goal last season - albeit an important one against Manchester City.
His record in the Champions League was much better, scoring six goals in his first seven matches in the competition last season - but consistency and confidence was lacking at the end of the campaign.
And Martinelli may be the player who takes the fall to improve Arsenal's overall transfer business. Any deal involving the Brazilian would surely break Arsenal's sale record - which has stood for nine years since Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain departed for Liverpool in 2017.
Arsenal need to sell better as a football club - does that start right now with the Brazilian?
Wright: Martinelli deserves to be treated with more respect
Former Arsenal striker Ian Wright speaking to Sky Sports:
"The way Martinelli is being treated at the moment, it really makes me feel uncomfortable.
"I know they might want him out, and a lot of people might say, 'yeah, it's time for him to move him on'. But there's ways of doing that and it should suit him as well, how he wants to leave.
"Not being involved in the squad, not being spoken to, he doesn't know what's going on. And yes, I know this - he doesn't know what is happening.
"He's done enough with this squad to be treated with a little bit more respect than he's being treated with at the moment.
"If you bring Vini in, Martinelli can say to himself, 'OK, they've brought him in, they've brought Tzolis in, I might be third [in the pecking order].
"But if you bring Tzolis in and have [Noni] Madueke on the other side, you're thinking to yourself, 'I can still have it with these two, I've got something to offer'. For him to be nowhere near it, it just makes me feel a bit sad for him."
summary: Arsenal and Al Hilal have made progress on a deal for Brazilian winger Gabriel Martinelli, with the player open to the move as a fee nears agreement. The potential transfer would break Arsenal's nine-year-old outgoing sales record and is expected to include a 20 percent sell-on clause on future profit. Meanwhile, Arsenal are weighing forward options before the transfer window closes, though potential targets like Julian Alvarez and Kenan Yildiz present complications.
key_points: Arsenal and Al Hilal have made progress on a transfer deal for Gabriel Martinelli.
Martinelli is seriously considering the move, and any agreement is expected to include a 20 per cent sell-on clause.
Martinelli previously turned down an approach from Turkish side Galatasaray.
Arsenal's potential replacement targets include Julian Alvarez and Kenan Yildiz, the latter of whom recently suffered a foot injury.
Martinelli has been at Arsenal since 2019 and won the Premier League with the club last season.

title: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Cole Palmer stars as Blues' superb front three edge pulsating contest in Xabi Alonso's first game
author: Ron Walker
content:
Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Cole Palmer stars as Blues' superb front three edge pulsating contest in Xabi Alonso's first game
Report and free match highlights as Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers all score to give Chelsea 3-2 victory at Fulham in Xabi Alonso's first game in charge; Alvaro Arbeloa's side punished for defensive lapses but Josh King and Goncalo Garcia take advantage of Robert Sanchez errors
Tuesday 25 August 2026 06:31, UK
Cole Palmer was back to his best to get Xabi Alonso's Chelsea career off to a winning start in a chaotic 3-2 victory at Fulham on Monday Night Football.
The Blues' attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers looked every bit the most potent in the Premier League as all three scored in a game where entertainment reigned and defending was an afterthought.
Palmer, finally injury-free and all the better for a summer off from England's World Cup campaign, scored one and made another in the kind of performance he had found so difficult to reproduce last season.
If his confidence on the pitch was not evidence enough, his response when Sky Sports asked how ready he was for the new season was emphatic. "Did you not watch the game?"
It took just 31 seconds for him to lay down a marker by teeing up an opener for Joao Pedro - himself refreshed after his surprise Brazil omission. The front three never looked back from there.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats | Watch FREE PL highlights
- Latest news and rumours: Fulham | Chelsea
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
Rogers got in on the act on debut with a late run to finish Maxence Lacroix's cross just before half-time, before his flick-on released Joao Pedro to set up Palmer for a third shortly after the break.
Chelsea would have had an easier night despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo without a nightmare performance from goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, whose mistakes twice let Fulham back into the game.
The Spaniard, whose position as the Blues' No 1 has long been questioned, let Josh King's powerful but saveable drive in at his near post to level matters midway through the opening period before spilling a shot straight into the path of Goncalo Garcia to allow Fulham to make it 3-2.
The first taste of the Alvaro Arbeloa era suggested the Cottagers will play on the front foot regardless of opposition and they created plenty against their west London rivals - but will need to significantly improve their defensive discipline after being cut wide open for each of Chelsea's goals.
On this evidence they will have score plenty too - and could have snatched a late equaliser when Antonee Robinson horribly miscued a chip with Sanchez in no man's land. But anything less than an away victory would have been harsh on Chelsea, who ran out deserved winners thanks to their electric front three.
Arbeloa: If we play like that, we'll win games
Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa on Sky Sports:
"It's a new project. Time is something we coaches don't have. But if we continue to play in that way, we're going to win a lot of games.
"I'm really happy and proud of my players, what I saw from them. This is the way I want to play. And we're going to play [this way] no matter who is in front of us."
Alonso refuses to criticise Sanchez despite errors
Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso on Sky Sports:
"It's not about talking about individuals, their situations. It's about understanding what it takes.
"For sure, the first goal we can do better than that. But it's a process. It's day one. And normally it's easier to learn with three points."
The key moments from Craven Cottage
1: GOAL! Lacroix's header from his own half splits Fulham's midfield before Palmer finds Joao Pedro to open the scoring after just 31 seconds.
23: GOAL! King's powerful drive goes through Sanchez at his near post to level for the hosts.
41: GOAL! Rogers' late run to the back post is found by Lacroix's cross and finished off by the record signing, who is left totally unmarked.
49: GOAL! Calvin Bassey needlessly pushes up and is beaten by Rogers to a flick-on towards Joao Pedro, who tees up Palmer to add a third.
54: GOAL! Goncalo Garcia nets his own debut goal as Sanchez pushes Castagne's effort straight at the summer signing.
65: BOO! Enzo Fernandez is met by huge jeers as he replaces Romeo Lavia after his antics for Argentina against England at the World Cup.
78: BIG CHANCE! With Sanchez off his line, Robinson's attempted chip lands well wide in a huge change to equalise.
82: INJURY? Shortly after telling the bench he needs to come off and pulling up mid-dribble, Palmer is replaced by Estevao.
summary: Cole Palmer starred with a goal and an assist as Chelsea defeated Fulham 3-2 in Xabi Alonso's first game in charge on Monday Night Football. Chelsea's front three of Palmer, Joao Pedro, and debutant Morgan Rogers all scored in an entertaining match where defensive errors from Blues goalkeeper Robert Sanchez let Fulham back into the game. Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham side showed attacking promise but were punished for defensive lapses, leaving Chelsea as deserving winners.
key_points: Chelsea won 3-2 against Fulham in Xabi Alonso's first match as manager.
The attacking trio of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, and debutant Morgan Rogers all scored for Chelsea.
Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez committed errors that allowed Josh King and Goncalo Garcia to score for Fulham.
Cole Palmer was substituted in the 82nd minute after appearing to signal an injury.

title: How many signings Liverpool will make before the transfer deadline REVEALED
author: Joe Williams
content:
![New Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola](https://d2x51gyc4ptf2q.cloudfront.net/content/uploads/2026/06/05102916/F365-Bournemouth-Manager-Andoni-Iraola-with-Liverpool-badge-1-1320x742.jpg) 
Sky Germany reporter Florian Plettenberg has revealed how many more signings Liverpool plan to make before the summer transfer window closes.
The Reds have signed Victor Munoz from Osasuna and Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes on permanent deals so far this summer, while Ronaldo Araujo has joined on a season-long loan deal from Barcelona.
Liverpool still feel they are short in attacking areas, especially in the wide positions and the Reds are now exploring a number of avenues as they look to navigate the final days of the summer transfer window.
Bradley Barcola is one of their key targets in the remaining days of the transfer market as they look to negotiate Paris Saint-Germain down from their original €170m asking price.
Giving an update on the situation on Monday, Italian transfer insider Fabrizio Romano said on his YouTube channel: “Don’t forget about Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye because both players once again are not part of the Paris Saint-Germain squad for the weekend.
“Bradley Barcola has been one of the sagas of the summer. If you are a friend of my YouTube channel, you heard Bradley Barcola to Liverpool since May, and I remain still super optimistic because Liverpool are working on it.
“There is a daily conversation with PSG. “I [didn’t] expect a breakthrough over the weekend. I always told you it’s going to be a slow deal.”
Before Romano added: “We are going to be in the final days of the summer transfer window, and that’s the case because it’s going to be next week and so I don’t know if it’s going to be on the line day or before, but the conversation is going to the very end.
“But Liverpool are absolutely on it.”
Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh is another player who Liverpool are looking to sign before the window shuts on September 1.
The Reds have already had two bids rejected for the Seagulls star with Gambian journalist Foday Manneh revealing a third offer is imminent, and may have already been lodged.
Manneh posted on X in early hours of Monday: ‘Yankuba Minteh to #LFC ; a 𝐓𝐇𝐈𝐑𝐃 𝐁𝐈𝐃 is expected to be sent to Brighton either tonight or Monday morning. They have discussed and are ready to go with an improved and convincing offer. The player continues to wait to formalise personal terms.’
Sky Germany reporter Plettenberg reckons there could even be a surprise third signing before the deadline as he reveals how many players Liverpool are likely to sign.
Plettenberg wrote on X: ‘Liverpool are planning to sign 2-3 more players before Deadline Day. Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh remain the top priorities for Liverpool at this stage. #LFC.’
READ NEXT: Winners and Losers: Maresca leaves Man Utd, De Zerbi, Villa and Isak to join Arteta
summary: Liverpool plan to secure two to three more signings before the summer transfer window closes on September 1. The club is actively pursuing attacking reinforcements, with Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh serving as their top priorities. Negotiations are ongoing with Paris Saint-Germain for Barcola, while a third bid is expected for Brighton's Minteh after previous offers were rejected.
key_points: Liverpool plan to make two to three additional signings before the transfer deadline.
Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh are Liverpool's top targets for the final days of the window.
Liverpool have already had two bids rejected for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh and are preparing a third.
Discussions with Paris Saint-Germain regarding Bradley Barcola are ongoing as Liverpool attempt to negotiate their €170m asking price.

title: Newcastle 2 Liverpool 2: Five Questions For The Reds To Answer
author: Josh Sexton
content:
Liverpool left it late to break Newcastle hearts again, so here are five questions The Reds still need to answer this summer…
SO, Liverpool left it late to break Newcastle hearts again.
However, given their opponents have been decimated in this transfer window, expectations before the game were that Andoni Iraola’s side would surely look the more put-together outfit of the two.
And yet it didn’t quite play out that way, so here are five questions The Reds still need to answer this summer, on the strength of yesterday’s evidence…
Jeremie Frimpong at right back
Milos Kerkez could rightly get as much criticism for his role in the first goal yesterday and for all too often being out of position, but adding to those likely tactical issues, Frimpong does have a real knack of looking particularly lightweight both in defence and attack.
For so much of yesterday he was completely outplayed and outmanned by Lewis Hall, while a lot of his passing and crossing when given space and time was undercooked, and he often looks all too easily overrun going the other way.
I liked him in between his injuries last season and thought he worked hard to make up for what he lacks in physical stature, but the current system as it is means he has to be able to be a right back that is strong going both ways, and I’m definitely concerned he might just not be able to rise to the level required.
The midfield balance
It’s closely linked to how the full backs operate, in that at the moment both are all or nothing, but having Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch operate as a double-pivot doesn’t seem like it’s a way home for Liverpool.
Yes, systemic things like this and possibly even the role of the fullbacks need time to be ironed out by the new manager, but to my mind it seems that Szoboszlai’s tendency to either chase the ball or get caught wrong side when attacks break down makes it more of a personnel issue.
Both were criticised in quarters for what they brought or didn’t bring to the midfield yesterday, but if I see Szoboszlai chase the ball down like a lunatic to pull out of a tackle and end up wrong side again I am going to blow a gasket.
Rio Ngumoha on the right
While he was still bright, and again may get better in the position given time, he was another that was completely outdone by Hall at left back yesterday.
He’s still young and has loads of time to add more strings to his bow, especially when learning a position, but he’ll have to learn to mix it up by coming inside sometimes and not just face up to take his man on before hitting the byline.
Of course, there’s a chance he doesn’t end up starting there much this season, but we’ll have more on that later…
Alexander Isak in isolation
Make no mistake, this was an immensely high-pressure game for him to come into, and no other will have the extra-curricular impact like playing at St. James’ Park. However, it all looked too familiar for Isak at Liverpool so far.
Isolated and unable to cover the ground required to get him on the ball more, and almost shocked and snatching at things when the ball did break for him, Andoni Iraola will need to – and as mentioned above, still could yet, of course – find a way to get The Reds’ number nine more involved.
He also needs to be more composed when things do break for him, though, as being a number nine in the Premier League against mostly low-block opponents can leave you feeding off scraps, and he has to meet his new manager in the middle if he’s to be a big success this season.
How many more moves?
It’s the question on everybody’s lips having seen just how much Liverpool were lacking in their first game, and yet there still seems to be a cautionary tale element to this question.
Three wingers have been strongly linked this window, with Yankuba Minteh the latest to see interest materialise into a bid, and some will argue all three would be nice and furthermore required if Cody Gakpo moves on.
Minteh and Ibrahim Mbaye would completely relieve Ngumoha of his right-wing responsibilities, while Bradley Barcola could be the main option off the left and even provide some Hugo Ekitike insurance through the middle until his counterpart recovers from an achilles injury.
How Victor Munoz, who too looked bright, fits into all of that remains to be seen and it’s clear Iraola is prepared to be flexible with his options as part of an altogether more fluid frontline.
That may in turn help bring Isak into things more too, but how it all fits together and the time that takes while Liverpool try to win games of football is the biggest question to answer of all wherever any aforementioned work within the squad still needs to be done.
summary: Following a late draw against Newcastle, Liverpool faces several tactical and personnel questions during the summer transfer window. Key concerns include the physical and defensive capabilities of right-back Jeremie Frimpong, midfield balance issues involving Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch, and how to better integrate striker Alexander Isak into the attack. Additionally, the club continues to weigh potential new signings to bolster the squad and support a more fluid frontline under the new manager.
key_points: Jeremie Frimpong struggled against Lewis Hall, raising concerns about his physical stature and ability to play effectively as a right-back.
Using Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch as a double-pivot created midfield balance issues for Liverpool.
Rio Ngumoha showed potential on the right wing but was outdone by Lewis Hall and needs to develop more tactical variety in his play.
Alexander Isak appeared isolated and struggled to get involved, highlighting the need for the manager to find ways to supply the number nine.
Liverpool is considering further transfer moves, with multiple wingers linked to the club to add depth and flexibility to the frontline.

title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott guilty of child sex abuse
author: James Delaney
content:
Snooker champion Graeme Dott guilty of child sex abuse
![PA Media Graeme Dott arriving at the High Court in Glasgow. He is wearing a dark suit over a pink shirt witha pink tie.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/b534/live/65133f90-9fc5-11f1-b3e7-331c6d9a8046.jpg.webp) PA Media
Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been found guilty of child sexual abuse.
The 49-year-old denied two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010.
During a trial, the High Court in Glasgow heard that Dott had exposed himself and inappropriately touched a primary school girl in the 1990s and attacked a young boy between 2006 and 2010.
Lord Harrower told Dott, who won the World Snooker Championship in 2006, he would be sentenced at a separate hearing in Edinburgh on 29 September.
Dott, from Glasgow, covered his face with his hands and shook his head while the verdict was delivered by jurors following a five-day trial.
![Getty Images Graeme Dott after winning the World Snooker Championship in 2006. He is holding his trophy in the air. It is silver and has green ribbons attached.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/4dcb/live/57d10030-9fc3-11f1-8648-8d7b77845e6d.jpg.webp) Getty Images
Lewd and libidinous practices refer to any sexual crimes against children committed prior to 1 December 2010.
The offence was abolished in 2009, but is still used for crimes carried out before then.
During the trial, the court heard how Dott had "caressed" the girl's bottom while giving her a piggyback and that, on another occasion, he had exposed himself to her.
On another occasion, she said Dott suggested she "take her trousers down" and lifted her top and began kissing her stomach after asking if she wanted to "play a guessing game".
The girl, now a woman in her 40s, said Dott would kiss her, touch her inappropriately and carried out a sexual act that would, if committed now, amount to rape.
She said she recalled the "smell" of creams Dott used for a skin condition after he kissed her and that the actions left her "shocked and scared".
'Rewarded' with gifts
The court heard how Dott bought her a teddy bear with a love heart on it in the course of the abuse.
The woman gave a new statement to police in 2025.
During his evidence, the boy said his abuse at the hands of Dott began not long after he defeated Peter Ebdon to win his sole world title at The Crucible in Sheffield in 2006.
The boy, now a man in his 20s, said he was about eight years old when Dott molested him in a shower at a home in South Lanarkshire.
He told the court how Dott "rewarded" him with crisps and fizzy drinks and once handed him a £50 note, only to accuse the boy of stealing it when his parents found out he had the money.
He also said he was abused in a car on a number of occasions and "inappropriately touched" while Dott played online poker.
Dott had told the trial the allegations were false and that he had "never acted inappropriately with anyone".
Det Insp Gary Smillie, of Police Scotland, described Dott as a "dangerous individual".
He added: "I hope this conviction provides some measure of comfort to those impacted by his crimes.
"His conviction is as a direct result of their strength in coming forward and providing information which assisted our inquiries."
Lord Harrower was told the woman had provided a victim impact statement for him to consider before sentencing next month.
Dott was taken into custody until then.
Removed from sport
The World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association (WPBSA) said it had permanently revoked Dott's membership with immediate effect.
This followed an emergency board meeting board where it was unanimously agreed to removed him from the sport.
The WPBSA has also written to World Snooker Tour (WST) to request his immediate removal from the WST Hall of Fame.
Dott was previously suspended from all professional snooker activities on 9 April 2025 pending the outcome of his trial.
He was subsequently relegated from the professional ranking list at the conclusion of the 2025/26 season.
summary: Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been found guilty at the High Court in Glasgow of child sexual abuse against a girl and a boy. The 49-year-old denied the two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour, which took place between 1993 and 2010. Dott was taken into custody and will be sentenced on 29 September in Edinburgh, while the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association has permanently revoked his membership.
key_points: Graeme Dott was found guilty of child sexual abuse following a five-day trial at the High Court in Glasgow.
The offenses involved a young girl in the 1990s and a young boy between 2006 and 2010.
Dott will be sentenced at a separate hearing in Edinburgh on 29 September and was taken into custody.
The World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association permanently revoked Dott's membership and requested his removal from the WST Hall of Fame.

title: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Cole Palmer stars as Blues' superb front three edge pulsating contest in Xabi Alonso's first game
author: Ron Walker
content:
Fulham vs Chelsea; Premier League
Fulham vs Chelsea. Premier League.
Craven Cottage.
Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Cole Palmer stars as Blues' superb front three edge pulsating contest in Xabi Alonso's first game
Report and free match highlights as Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers all score to give Chelsea 3-2 victory at Fulham in Xabi Alonso's first game in charge; Alvaro Arbeloa's side punished for defensive lapses but Josh King and Goncalo Garcia take advantage of Robert Sanchez errors
Monday 24 August 2026 23:42, UK
Cole Palmer was back to his best to get Xabi Alonso's Chelsea career off to a winning start in a chaotic 3-2 victory at Fulham on Monday Night Football.
The Blues' attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers looked every bit the most potent in the Premier League as all three scored in a game where entertainment reigned and defending was an afterthought.
Palmer, finally injury-free and all the better for a summer off from England's World Cup campaign, scored one and made another in the kind of performance he had found so difficult to reproduce last season.
If his confidence on the pitch was not evidence enough, his response when Sky Sports asked how ready he was for the new season was emphatic. "Did you not watch the game?"
It took just 31 seconds for him to lay down a marker by teeing up an opener for Joao Pedro - himself refreshed after his surprise Brazil omission. The front three never looked back from there.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats | Watch FREE PL highlights
- Latest news and rumours: Fulham | Chelsea
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
Rogers got in on the act on debut with a late run to finish Maxence Lacroix's cross just before half-time, before his flick-on released Joao Pedro to set up Palmer for a third shortly after the break.
Chelsea would have had an easier night despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo without a nightmare performance from goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, whose mistakes twice let Fulham back into the game.
The Spaniard, whose position as the Blues' No 1 has long been questioned, let Josh King's powerful but saveable drive in at his near post to level matters midway through the opening period before spilling a shot straight into the path of Goncalo Garcia to allow Fulham to make it 3-2.
The first taste of the Alvaro Arbeloa era suggested the Cottagers will play on the front foot regardless of opposition and they created plenty against their west London rivals - but will need to significantly improve their defensive discipline after being cut wide open for each of Chelsea's goals.
On this evidence they will have score plenty too - and could have snatched a late equaliser when Antonee Robinson horribly miscued a chip with Sanchez in no man's land. But anything less than an away victory would have been harsh on Chelsea, who ran out deserved winners thanks to their electric front three.
Arbeloa: If we play like that, we'll win games
Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa on Sky Sports:
"It's a new project. Time is something we coaches don't have. But if we continue to play in that way, we're going to win a lot of games.
"I'm really happy and proud of my players, what I saw from them. This is the way I want to play. And we're going to play [this way] no matter who is in front of us."
Alonso refuses to criticise Sanchez despite errors
Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso on Sky Sports:
"It's not about talking about individuals, their situations. It's about understanding what it takes.
"For sure, the first goal we can do better than that. But it's a process. It's day one. And normally it's easier to learn with three points."
The key moments from Craven Cottage
1: GOAL! Lacroix's header from his own half splits Fulham's midfield before Palmer finds Joao Pedro to open the scoring after just 31 seconds.
23: GOAL! King's powerful drive goes through Sanchez at his near post to level for the hosts.
41: GOAL! Rogers' late run to the back post is found by Lacroix's cross and finished off by the record signing, who is left totally unmarked.
49: GOAL! Calvin Bassey needlessly pushes up and is beaten by Rogers to a flick-on towards Joao Pedro, who tees up Palmer to add a third.
54: GOAL! Goncalo Garcia nets his own debut goal as Sanchez pushes Castagne's effort straight at the summer signing.
65: BOO! Enzo Fernandez is met by huge jeers as he replaces Romeo Lavia after his antics for Argentina against England at the World Cup.
78: BIG CHANCE! With Sanchez off his line, Robinson's attempted chip lands well wide in a huge change to equalise.
82: INJURY? Shortly after telling the bench he needs to come off and pulling up mid-dribble, Palmer is replaced by Estevao.
summary: Cole Palmer starred with a goal and an assist as Chelsea defeated Fulham 3-2 in Xabi Alonso's first game in charge on Monday Night Football. Chelsea's front three of Palmer, Joao Pedro, and debutant Morgan Rogers all scored to secure the victory at Craven Cottage. Meanwhile, two errors from Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez allowed Josh King and Goncalo Garcia to keep Fulham in the contest.
key_points: Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, and Morgan Rogers all scored for Chelsea in their 3-2 victory over Fulham.
The match marked Xabi Alonso's first game in charge of Chelsea and Alvaro Arbeloa's first game in charge of Fulham.
Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez made two costly errors that allowed Josh King and Goncalo Garcia to score for Fulham.
Joao Pedro opened the scoring for Chelsea after just 31 seconds following an assist from Palmer.

title: Man utd open talks for Alejandro Balde as Red Devils have contacted Barcelona star's camp over shock summer transfer | Goal.com UK
author: Donny Afroni
content:
![Udinese v Barcelona: Friuli Venezia Giulia Cup](https://assets.goal.com/images/v3/getty-2289730628/crop/MM5DEMRXGI5DCMRXHA5G433XMU5DGNZWHIZDOMI=/GettyImages-2289730628.jpg?auto=webp&format=pjpg&width=3840&quality=60) Getty Images Sport
- Red Devils seek defensive coverMan Utd have officially registered their interest in Balde as the club looks to solve their long-standing issues on the left side of the defence. According to ESPN, Old Trafford officials have reportedly reached out to the player's camp to gauge his interest in a move to the Premier League before the summer transfer window slams shut. The Red Devils had previously been linked with Newcastle United full-back Lewis Hall earlier in the window, but the focus has now shifted toward the 22-year-old Spaniard as a premium alternative to their current options. The urgency behind United's pursuit stems from ongoing concerns regarding Luke Shaw's durability. While the England international remains the first-choice option when fit, there are internal worries that he may struggle to cope with the physical demands of playing three games a week across both the Premier League and the Champions League. Shaw started every league game last season, but at 31, his history of muscular injuries has forced the United hierarchy to look for a younger, more explosive talent who can share the workload.
- ![alejandro Balde](https://assets.goal.com/images/v3/blt5d9665bc9ca276e0/crop/MM5DCOBZG45DCMBWG45G433XMU5DSMZTHI2DKMI=/GettyImages-2290762539.jpg?auto=webp&format=pjpg&width=3840&quality=60) (C)Getty Images Man Utd propose loan-to-buy dealShould the Spanish international express a formal desire to leave the Camp Nou, Man Utd are prepared to structure a deal that suits their current financial constraints. The club would prefer to negotiate a season-long loan deal that includes an option to make the move permanent next summer. This approach would allow United to assess Balde's adaptation to English football before committing a significant portion of their budget. However, Barcelona's financial situation means they may prefer an immediate sale to balance their books, with the club valuing the La Masia graduate at between £26 million and £34m. The negotiations are expected to be complex, as Barcelona are not under immediate pressure to sell one of their brightest young talents unless the player forces a move. Balde is said to be keen on a face-to-face meeting with Flick to understand exactly where he stands in the pecking order.
- Flick addresses Balde omissionSpeculation regarding Balde's future reached fever pitch after he was surprisingly left out of the squad for Barcelona's 5-0 win over Elche on Sunday. Flick was quick to address the situation, suggesting that the player’s mental state was the primary reason for his absence. "We have to manage the minutes, I hope to have six players who can play 90 minutes," Flick told reporters. "I spoke with Balde this morning and told him that I think he's not here at 100 per cent, clear your mind and then we'll talk." Despite the emphatic victory for the Catalan giants, Balde’s absence remained the talking point. Flick has insisted that the player's talent is not the issue, but rather his current focus and commitment to the project. He stated: "He’s a player of immense quality, and it’s important to know if he’s confident he can compete in his position. That’s what I want to see from all my players. Every day I observe what they do, their level, whether they demonstrate that they’re at the level to play."
- ![FC Barcelona v RCD Espanyol de Barcelona - LaLiga EA Sports](https://assets.goal.com/images/v3/getty-2271000398/crop/MM5DEMZVHA5DCMZSGY5G433XMU5DIMZTHIZDGNI=/GettyImages-2271000398.jpg?auto=webp&format=pjpg&width=3840&quality=60) Getty Images Sport Competition and injury historyWhile Balde is undoubtedly a high-ceiling talent, his recent injury record is something that Man Utd's medical staff will be monitoring closely. For a club like United, which has been plagued by defensive injuries over the last two years, ensuring that Balde can maintain his fitness in the more physical Premier League environment will be a priority. As the clock ticks down toward the end of the transfer window, Man Utd are remaining patient but have made it clear to all parties that they are ready to act.

summary: Manchester United has opened talks with Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde's camp to address ongoing concerns regarding Luke Shaw's durability on the left side of their defense. United is reportedly considering a season-long loan deal with an option to buy, though Barcelona may prefer an immediate sale valued between £26 million and £34 million. Speculation over Balde's future intensified after he was left out of Barcelona's recent squad due to concerns over his mental state and focus, as addressed by manager Hansi Flick.
key_points: Manchester United has registered interest in Barcelona's 22-year-old left-back Alejandro Balde.
United's pursuit is driven by concerns over 31-year-old Luke Shaw's history of muscular injuries and the physical demands of playing multiple competitions.
Manchester United prefers a season-long loan deal with an option to buy, while Barcelona may favor an immediate sale valued at £26 million to £34 million.
Balde was recently left out of Barcelona's squad for a match against Elche, with manager Hansi Flick citing concerns over the player's mental state and 100 percent focus.

title: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Rogers and Palmer star as Sanchez struggles - how the players rated
author: Nizaar Kinsella
content:
![Chelsea's Morgan Rogers produces a "cold" celebration made famous by Cole Palmer as he scores against Fulham in the Premier League](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/819/cpsprodpb/613f/live/4530ea30-9ffa-11f1-be19-71b839ccdc73.jpg)
Morgan Rogers scored 41 minutes into his Premier League debut for Chelsea
- Published
Morgan Rogers scored on his Chelsea debut as Xabi Alonso's side beat Fulham at Craven Cottage.
The Â£117m signing slotted in his side's second goal after Fulham midfielder Josh King had cancelled out Joao Pedro's opener, which came within 31 seconds.
Cole Palmer thought he had sealed victory for Chelsea with a third goal early in the second half before debutant striker Gonzalo Garcia gave Fulham hope but the visitors held on to start the season with a win.
Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them at the bottom of the page too.
Fulham ratings
Bernd Leno: The German goalkeeper was not particularly at fault for any of Chelsea's goals but still couldn't stop them. 5
Timothy Castagne: The right-back set up King's goal and his shot led to Fulham's second, but he struggled defensively. 6
Jorge Cuenca: His poor clearance and mistimed tackle led to Chelsea's opening goal. He was also at fault for the second, failing to stop Lacroix's cross. However, his lofted pass helped create Fulham's second goal. 4
Calvin Bassey: Less culpable than many of his defensive team-mates, but still part of a disappointing display at the back. 5
Antonee Robinson: The United States international produced an important early block from a Rogers effort and delivered an excellent cross later in the first half, but was often caught out of position on the counter-attack. He lofted a finish well wide in the 77th minute with his weaker right foot when one-on-one with Sanchez. 6
Sander Berge: Struggled to dictate the tempo as he had done in pre-season in an unsettled game. 5
Josh King: The academy graduate was Fulham's standout performer, creating chances and posing a threat before scoring the first-half equaliser. Almost produced an equaliser in the 73rd minute from range. 8
Alex Iwobi: The Nigeria international provided a strong physical presence both defensively and in attack. 6
Oscar Bobb: The Norway international's direct running caused problems down the right, although his influence faded as the game wore on. 7
Gonzalo Garcia: On his debut, Garcia provided a useful focal point in attack in a difficult match for Fulham. He helped relieve pressure after long spells of Chelsea possession and was rewarded with a close-range header in the second half. 7
Cesar Palacios: The new signing worked hard on his debut, but little came off for him, including a long-range effort that flew well over the bar in the first half. 5
Subs:
Shea Charles (on 67, Bobb): The new signing from Southampton produced some dangerous long balls as Fulham pushed for an equaliser. 6
Kevin (on 73, Palacios): Did little to influence the game. 5
Ryan Sessegnon (on 73, Berge): His running in-behind threatened down the left and he forced a good save from Sanchez. 6
Rodrigo Muniz (on 82, Robinson): 5
Subs not used: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Kevin, Smith Rowe.
Chelsea ratings
Robert Sanchez: An early kicking error gifted Fulham a corner. He should have saved King's equaliser at his near post, while his initial save for Fulham's second was parried into a dangerous area, allowing Garcia to score. 3
Josh Acheampong: The 20-year-old produced a fine double clearance and block in the 27th minute and looked solid throughout. 6
Maxence Lacroix: Remarkably involved in both of Chelsea's first two goals, with his headed clearance leading to the opener and his run down the right and cut-back setting up Rogers. 7
Levi Colwill: An early mistake left him fortunate to escape with only a yellow card after a foul on Bobb. He was also partly at fault for Fulham's second goal after failing to clear a deep cross. 5
Malo Gusto: The wing-back was a surprise selection amid Chelsea's injury problems, but his passing lacked conviction at times. 5
Romeo Lavia: Booked early on after a late challenge on Bassey. He grew into the game, however, going close from a corner and moving the ball well through midfield. 5
Reece James: Saw a miscued effort saved in the first half but gradually grew into the game and helped Chelsea gain control. 6
Jorrel Hato: Operating in an unfamiliar wing-back role, the defender produced a promising early dribble and adapted well. 6
Cole Palmer: Simply the best player on the pitch. Palmer was creative, physically impressive and produced several superb dribbles before scoring an excellent third goal. He looks refreshed after the summer break. 9
Morgan Rogers: An outstanding debut. Pressed aggressively, had a shot blocked, played in Joao Pedro and then capped his display by scoring Chelsea's second with a far-post finish. 8
Joao Pedro: Opened the scoring after 31 seconds with a deft finish over Leno. He also exploited Fulham's high defensive line intelligently to set up Palmer's goal. 8
Subs:
Enzo Fernandez (on 65, Lavia): The Argentine was booed by the home fans on every touch of the ball and might not have featured had Moises Caicedo been fit. Still, Fernandez moved the ball around the pitch and fought for possession. 6
Pep Chavarria (on 65, Hato): It was a back-to-the-wall job for the wing-back but he did little of note on his brief debut cameo. 5
Pedro Neto (on 76, Gusto): 5
Geovany Quenda (on 82, Rogers): 5
Estevao (on 83, Palmer): 5
Subs not used: Penders, Barco, Gittens, Welbeck.
How did you rate the players?
How to play
Rate players out of 10 for this game. The rater will close 30 minutes after the final whistle. You must be signed in to a BBC account to play.
Substitutes
Substitutes
After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.
summary: Chelsea defeated Fulham 3-2 away at Craven Cottage in their opening Premier League match of the season. Joao Pedro opened the scoring within 31 seconds before Josh King equalized for Fulham, but debutant Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer scored to secure the victory for Xabi Alonso's side. Gonzalo Garcia scored a late header for Fulham, but Chelsea held on to claim all three points.
key_points: Joao Pedro scored the opening goal for Chelsea just 31 seconds into the match.
Debutants Morgan Rogers and Gonzalo Garcia both scored for their respective teams.
Cole Palmer scored Chelsea's third goal early in the second half to help secure the victory.
Fulham's Josh King scored an equalizer in the first half and was his side's standout performer.

title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
author: Nick Ames
content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.
The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.
Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.
“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.
“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”
The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”
Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.
One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.
after newsletter promotion
“I don’t think that [Infantino] has done anything wrong,” he said. “All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.
“I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After president Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”
summary: A group of influential current and former footballers, including prominent figures with ties to Fifa, have demanded change at the top of Fifa and urged Gianni Infantino to face pressure to resign. The backlash was sparked by Infantino's attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup, with players and fans criticizing the leadership for lacking consultation and drifting from the sport's core values. Meanwhile, Infantino has resisted the resignation calls, and figures like Samuel Eto'o have defended him, attributing the criticism to the upcoming election.
key_points: Current and former footballers released a statement demanding leadership change at Fifa and criticizing Gianni Infantino.
Signatories include notable players such as Mikaël Silvestre, Lucy Bronze, David James, and Emmanuel Petit.
The backlash was triggered by Infantino's ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.
Gianni Infantino has resisted calls to resign and has been seeking support from smaller member associations.
Samuel Eto'o defended Infantino, stating he has done nothing wrong and that the criticism is tied to the upcoming election.

title: Fulham vs Chelsea live: Score and latest updates from Premier League
author: Kieran Crichard; Sam Wallace; Matt Law
content:
![Joao Pedro scores](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499453493_17875985377580_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqMNRDlTuMi-XjpR1_E2e8HIKKdcOWYOPgRv3NQ685lJs.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Joao Pedro scores](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499453493_17875985377580_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqMNRDlTuMi-XjpR1_E2e8HIKKdcOWYOPgRv3NQ685lJs.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
14 mins: Fulham 0 Chelsea 1
Chelsea started this game well but have lost control and are asking for trouble. The latest example sees Sanchez take too long to clear and he accidentally allows the ball to go out before clearing to gift Fulham a corner. Bobb’s delivery is headed away at the near post by James.
12 mins: Fulham 0 Chelsea 1
That is strong one-vs-one defending from Bassey. Palmer lifts the ball over the top to pick out the run of Pedro, who is dispossessed inside the Fulham box by Bassey.
Moments later, Lavia flies into a reckless challenge on Bassey and is booked. Lavia looks stunned at that decision but he is perhaps on the fortunate side that VAR did not advise the referee to have a further look at that on the screen. Lavia was out of control and could have easily been in more trouble. Two Chelsea players already into the book and were a little bit lucky.
5 mins: Fulham 0 Chelsea 1
Colwill is in trouble. Could Chelsea go down to 10 men early? He loses possession poorly inside his own half and then resorts to hacking Bobb down with a nasty challenge. Was Colwill the last man and could Bobb have gone racing in on goal? Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.
GOAL! Pedro puts Chelsea in front after 30 seconds
With their first attack of the Xabi Alonso era, Chelsea hit the front inside the opening minute of this west London derby. Lacroix’s header from halfway finds Palmer, who plays it into the path of Pedro. The Brazilian, fresh from signing a new deal at the club, takes it in his stride and, from inside the Fulham penalty area, lifts it over Leno and into the far corner. A fine finish from Pedro and Alonso has the perfect start.
Could Joao Pedro be the man to finally lift the curse of the number nine shirt at Chelsea? Liam Delap tried and failed last season. Pedro has taken it this term and has started like a train with that early goal. Pedro has also been prolific in pre-season and has been widely tipped to be one of the Premier League’s top scorers.
Kick-off
Before we get going, we take a moment to remember the great Kevin Keegan, who managed Fulham in the late 1990s.
We are under way at Craven Cottage in the final game on this opening weekend of the new Premier League season.
Alvaro Arbeloa is out on the pitch for the first time in the Premier League. A friendly if not rapturous welcome from the home fans. He’s rolled his sleeves up and he’s ready to go - literally, his skinny fit jacket has sleeves rolled up tight. It looks quite uncomfortable.
It might be a new season and a new manager, but Chelsea are still doing their pre-match huddle. Fortunately, it was nowhere near the referee or the centre circle. It seemed to be captain Reece James doing all the talking.
Nearly ready for action
Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Craven Cottage and we are moments away from kick-off in this west London derby. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up tonight:
Fulham: Leno; Castagne, Cuenca, Bassey, Robinson, King, Berge, Iwobi; Bobb, Garcia, Palacios.
Substitutes: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Charles, Sessegnon, Kevin, Smith Rowe, Muniz.
Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.
Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.
The boos for Fernandez from the Fulham fans got a lot louder when the players stepped on the pitch. Some people chanted something rather nasty beginning with ‘w’ as well.
Enzo booed
There were a few boos from the Fulham fans when Enzo Fernandez’s name was read out ahead of kick-off. Clearly the England fans at Craven Cottage haven’t forgotten what happened against Argentina. Fernandez was booed by some Chelsea supporters in pre-season, but there were no loud jeers from the away end during the team announcements.
summary: Chelsea defeated Fulham in a west London derby opening match of the Premier League season under new manager Xabi Alonso. Joao Pedro scored the opening goal for Chelsea within the first minute of the game. Both Colwill and Lavia received early yellow cards for reckless challenges during a lively start to the match.
key_points: Joao Pedro scored Chelsea's opening goal in the first minute of the match.
Chelsea players Colwill and Lavia both received early yellow cards for challenges.
The match took place at Craven Cottage as the final game of the opening Premier League weekend.
Enzo Fernandez received boos from Fulham fans prior to kick-off.

Fulham vs Chelsea preview
The last two managers of Real Madrid before current boss Jose Mourinho took over at the Bernabeu were Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and Chelsea’s Xabi Alonso and both will be seeking a strong start to their new Premier League roles in this London derby.
Getting quickly out of the blocks will be of greater importance to Alonso, who is Chelsea’s tenth different permanent or interim manager over the last decade and has seen the club spend £348 million over the summer.
Arbeloa has big shoes to fill as Marco Silva had turned Fulham into an established mid-table side before leaving for Benfica and they have lost some seasoned players too, after Raul Jimenez, Sasa Lukic, Issa Diop and Harry Wilson all departed Craven Cottage.
He has turned to youth to bolster his squad, bringing in familiar faces Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios from Real Madrid, while paying a big fee to Southampton for the exciting Shea Charles.
However, with Joachim Andersen suspended and Tom Cairney injured, there appears to be a lack of leaders and experience in Arbeloa's ranks and it is still early days in the Spaniard's managerial career.
Chelsea, having finished tenth last season, will be demanding much more and Alonso will want nothing but a winning start in this capital clash.
With no European commitments, the Blues could be the side to give Arsenal and Manchester City most to think about in the Premier League title race and in Cole Palmer, new boy Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro, they have an array of attacking talent at their disposal.
Having Levi Colwill back in a new-look defence alongside Maxence Lacroix should ensure things are solid at the back and they get plenty of protection in midfield from Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo.
There is a lot of guesswork involved given the mass of change in both camps, so treading carefully in the match markets is advised, and Pedro could be the star of the show.
Pedro arrived at Stamford Bridge from Brighton as more of a ten but he has made the number nine position his own at Chelsea and was invaluable last season, scoring 15 goals and getting eight assists in 35 Premier League appearances.
Being left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad could be a blessing in disguise and he has been in prolific form in pre-season, scoring a hat-trick against Western Sydney Wanderers before braces against Milan and Real Sociedad.
The club announced the 24-year-old had signed a deal until 2034 on Saturday and he should thrive off the even greater service provided by the arrival of Rogers.
Pedro can celebrate the news by getting off the mark and he has scored in two of his last three clashes with the Cottagers.
Card calling for Cuenca
Last season’s meeting between Fulham and Chelsea at Craven Cottage was a fiery affair featuring three yellow cards apiece and a sending off for now-former Blue Marc Cucurella.
One of those bookings was for Fulham centre-back Jorge Cuenca and, with Andersen suspended and Diop having moved on, he is almost certain to start at the back.
Cuenca was carded six times last season in just 938 minutes of action and Chelsea’s fluid frontline are quick in transitions, which could leave the Spaniard vulnerable.
