title: Julián Alvarez walks alone at Atlético in transfer saga with no end – and no winners | Sid Lowe
author: Sid Lowe
content:
Julián Alvarez entered a long, dark tunnel on his own. “We’re stronger together,” Giuliano Simeone said but that wasn’t the way it went. At the end of their first home game of the season, a 2-2 draw with Villarreal, all of Atlético Madrid’s players gathered by the centre circle, shook hands with their opponents and each other, then headed towards the south end of the Metropolitano. Almost all of them did, anyway: one was left behind. Somebody in a suit had a quiet word then the press officer came, pointing in the other direction. So, while his teammates turned to the supporters who had turned on him, the man wearing No 19 went west, to the exit.
Alvarez walked alone. Head down in silence, as he had been all afternoon and beyond, he set off slowly across the pitch accompanied only by his thoughts and the whistles that followed him. Not offered a hand to shake or a nod of acknowledgment, he stepped past the Atlético badge on the touchline where the mouth of the tunnel opens. Either side, supporters hung over the void, whistling and shouting. Way off to his left, Atlético’s other players paused, seemingly waiting for him to slip out of sight before approaching the stand, but none turned back. A scarf was thrown, landing at Alvarez’s feet and left lying there. And then he disappeared into the dark, a portrait of the place he is in.
No one was waiting for him on the other side. Alvarez went up the stairs, past a couple of security guards and turned left to an empty dressing room, not lifting his gaze and not invited to either. Four minutes would pass before his teammates came up the stairs together. But at least it was quiet now, for a little while. The noise had been loud; no one could recall supporters turning on their own player quite like this. Atlético’s fans, still his fans, had whistled him when his name was read out, whistled him when he had warmed up, whistled him when he came on wearing red and white there for the first time since April and since he declared it his “dream” to leave, and they had whistled him out of there too, for good.
Good? “Unhappily, this situation isn’t comfortable for anyone,” Jan Oblak said, and amid the damage done, the mutual accusations, the hurt pride and spited faces, nor is it easy to see a solution. The situation, in short, is this: Julián Alvarez wants to leave for Barcelona. Barcelona want to sign him. But he has a contract until June 2030, a €500m buyout clause, and Atlético won’t sell him. And definitely not to them. And so, here they are. Stuck.
![Julián Alvarez trudges off the pitch alone as his Atlético Madrid teammates applaud the fans.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/60e0447bf266cbef343b6702396ac674a380eaa3/0_0_4132_2755/master/4132.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The first time Alvarez hinted he may not continue was after facing Tottenham in the Champions League last March. The timing seemed odd then: it hadn’t been an easy season, the feeling that something was wrong growing and about to be confirmed, but he had just scored twice and Atlético had won 5-2. It seemed odder still when he chose the moments after Argentina beat Austria at the World Cup to announce he wanted to go. “It’s not the time to talk about this but nor can I hide,” he said. “I spoke with the people I needed to [at Atlético] and the best thing for everyone is a transfer. I want to fulfil my dream.”
There had been a “bid” that wasn’t really a bid at all from Real Madrid but the dream was Barcelona and they were the ones who had been speaking to Alvarez, planning how to make it happen. Which was one of the reasons why Atlético were so determined it wouldn’t, deciding to take a stand instead, make this a cause. This was not about him wanting to go, or not only, but about the way it had been done.
From New York, Joan Laporta claimed that Barcelona had made an “important” offer. “If Atlético are prepared to accept, fantastic,” he said, but they weren’t and they didn’t think much of the offer either. Atlético’s chief executive, Miguel Ángel Gil Marín, insisted they would not sell at any price: they had told Alvarez, his agent and Barcelona that. “I know Joan: he’s always acting up for the media, fans, his own personal circus,” Gil Marín said. “I told him: ‘Leave it, please. We don’t want to sell and won’t sell, stop insisting’. He loves to play the part but he knows perfectly well that Julián won’t play for Barcelona next season.”
Barcelona insisted that they had approached a potential transfer the right way, with “respect”, but Atlético reported them to the RFEF (Spanish Football Federation) and refused to budge, a statement made, territory defended. This had become a point of principle, examples to be made of them. The noise though refused to go away. When Alvarez arrived for pre-season, still wanting out, he cut an isolated figure. If every silence and furrowed brow was analysed to death, it was true that there was an absence about him. This weekend Jorge Valdano took a line from Julio Cortázar to explain it: “When someone says they’re going, they’re already gone.”
Even if they’re not going. While Atlético quietly investigated other options, Gil Marín gave a statement again insisting that Alvarez was staying. “We can’t allow other clubs and media to dictate our policy and disrespect us,” he said. “We have values.” He attacked Alvarez’s agent too, saying that Alvarez had been poorly advised. To which Fernando Hidalgo – whose version has Atlético promising that if Alvarez publicly said he wanted to go, taking responsibility, they would allow him to – replied with a post: “Never ask a liar to explain why he lied; he would only have to lie again.”
As for the coach, watching his superiors take the lead, he was ready to put Alvarez back in the team. “You can’t be clearer than the club’s been. It’s like when the judge says: ‘Denied!’,” Simeone said. As if it was that simple, the case so easily dismissed. While Atlético said they would “look after” him, while accusing Barcelona and Hidalgo lifted some blame from his shoulders, Alvarez’s return instead underlined that coming back from this might be even harder than anticipated, redemption more of a reach than imagined.
![Diego Simeone stands in front of his substitutes.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/dcf93f70b9e68c9bfe7a240dc5cc6fac72966ce1/0_0_4489_2993/master/4489.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Sunday did not suggest a solution, a moment for the healing to start. Instead, it felt unsustainable, the case eclipsing all else, pressure building to find a proper conclusion. This was a fun match, but it was all about one man, the bad guy, and the verdict against him – and that affects everyone, maybe no winners any more. After the game there was a moment when, hands raised in front of him, the press officer asked journalists if there were any more questions, pausing to add … about the game … and the hands went down again. Before it, every photographer gathered in front of the bench as Alvarez took up his place to the left of Juan Musso and José María Gimenez, staring at the floor, the only movement his clenching jaw, while 60,000 people whistled his name. That, it turned out, was just the beginning.
Quick Guide
La Liga results
Rayo Vallecano 1-1 Alavés, Real Betis 1-0 Real Sociedad, Espanyol 1-2 Real Madrid, Valencia 0-0 Celta Vigo, Athletic Club 1-3 Sevilla, Elche 0-5 Barcelona, Getafe 1-0 Racing de Santander, Atlético Madrid 2-2 Villarreal
When he went to warm up on 51 minutes, they whistled again. From the south end, there were chants of “Fuck Barcelona! Fuck Catalonia!” They sang: “We are Atlético”. And “Atlético yes, mercenaries no!” Another one ran: “Tell him to go, once and for fucking all!” (To which Alvarez might have thought: yeah, that’s what I’m trying to do). As Atlético’s players came to the touchline after their first goal, the fitness coach said Alvarez was about to go on. “Careful, eh,” Marc Pubill replied. The noise when he did was deafening and didn’t relent. There weren’t many touches but with every one the angry volume rose, the rejection not receding all the way to the final whistle, which was not the final whistle at all: that too was for Alvarez. With eight days left in the window, it could still have been a good riddance, but … if it’s not?
“Julián is with us in the team and for as long as he is, we’re going to support him,” Oblak said. “All I know is that if Atlético want to win titles we have to be together, we need strikers and we need important strikers,” Simeone noted, admitting he had apologised to Ademola Lookman for making him play there in the absence of Alvarez and the injured Alex Sørloth. They do have strikers, the coach said the second time he turned to that line, but they would have to “take care” of them, the coach confirming that the club had told him it was their decision that he shouldn’t greet the fans, not Julián’s.
Yet if it had been designed to protect Alvarez and if this statement had too, absolving him of having chosen to turn his back on them, it also exposed him. Leaving first without the others, none joining him, served as an expression of his isolation, his othering, of how broken the situation had become. “Together we’re stronger, that’s always characterised us, made Atlético Madrid different. He is our player so we will die for him on the pitch,” Giuliano said, but when the time came, Alvarez went alone.

title: Man Utd: Why there shouldn't be panic after Michael Carrick's side suffered Premier League loss at Hull on opening day
author: Danyal Khan
content:
Man Utd: Why there shouldn't be panic after Michael Carrick's side suffered Premier League loss at Hull on opening day
Michael Carrick saw his Manchester United side beaten by promoted Hull City on the opening day of the new Premier League season; Dan Khan tells us why it's not time to panic at Old Trafford yet; Man Utd host Ipswich, live on Sky on Sunday; kick off at 4.30pm
Monday 24 August 2026 17:17, UK
I was at the game on Saturday and it was clear early on in the game that Manchester United were not at the races against Hull City.
Words will be bandied towards Michael Carrick's side this week until their home game against Ipswich on Sunday; for example, a lack of intensity, aggression and intent on display.
But when I left Hull, I just felt it was a bit more nuanced than that.

- Man Utd fixtures & scores | FREE Man Utd highlights▶️
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
It was a bad performance, for sure. Carrick's side didn't perform, and only he will truly know why, but from the off it was quite clear some of his main players are not quite up to match sharpness compared to where they will be in a few weeks.
Six of Carrick's first-team players did have a full pre-season. But Carrick also had a new midfield duo playing together in Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.
Off the bench, he had players nowhere near full fitness in Benjamin Sesko (has not played a minute of pre-season), as well as Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford, who have had limited minutes since returning from England duty in the summer.
Hull also deserve enormous credit for being a well-drilled outfit for their first Premier League game in nine years while also having a squad who have experienced a full pre-season to prepare for their opener.
Also, allow me a moment to myth-bust something I have seen across social media over the last few days since the defeat.
'Four defeats out of five under Michael Carrick have come against sides who have played a back five'
Not having it. Look at the games!
Two of them were pre-season games, including United's first of the summer against Wrexham and their last against Ruben Amorim's AC Milan. If anyone is using these as barometers of a side struggling against a formation, it is simply not right.
Hull was bad. Leeds at Old Trafford last season was also bad. These two performances share a lot of similarities but I would argue the most common denominator is that I left both games thinking they were seriously lacking from a physical point of view and that will be Carrick's most pressing thought.
I am more than willing, and Carrick has more than deserved, somewhat of a pass for the Hull result, and I would be extremely surprised if United were not considerably improved against Ipswich Town on Sunday.
So what are Man Utd's plans for the remainder of the transfer window?
The midfield was Manchester United's priority going into the season and they have gone some way to addressing it by spending over £150m in reinforcements, with Carlos Baleba the latest addition to their ranks.
But United find themselves in a similar situation to last summer - reinforcing your greatest need just highlights your next biggest gap within the squad.
Rewind back to 2025: the club had finally addressed their inefficiency up front by adding Benjamin Sesko, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo but having sorted the attacking weaponry, it became even more obvious the midfield needed strengthening.
United waited 12 months as they did not want to sign a stop-gap midfielder for the sake of addressing the area and believed they would have a better run at the midfield market the following summer.
There is a similar feeling now when it comes to left-back. Now United have signed their three midfielders, the need for a left-back is a must.
The club have long admired Myles Lewis-Skelly and Lewis Hall and my feeling is they are top of United's list in that position.
Both seem unattainable at this moment in time, with managers of both clubs dismissing any chances of their players leaving. In addition to Bruno Guimaraes' injury, which especially seems to all but rule out a potential departure for Lewis-Skelly.
My feeling is that with United having focused on attack and midfield over the last two summer windows, they are willing to wait until next summer to address their defence - including a first-choice left-back when Luke Shaw's contract expires next summer.
Things could change of course, and I would not completely rule out United getting creative in terms of potentially adding a left-back in the last week of the window but at the moment, it seems unlikely.
Barcelona's Alejandro Balde has been the latest player linked with United at left-back but from what I understand, although United are aware of his situation in Catalonia, it is not a name they are strongly pursuing at this time.
All in all, it is a lot of pressure on Luke Shaw to stay fit all season, and some reliance will need to be put on Patrick Dorgu at left-back. The club see his long-term future in that position.
Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot can also both deputise in that position too.
In terms of departures at United, at the time of writing, it seems unlikely any first-team players will leave the club before the deadline.
One potential departure this window was Dutch forward Joshua Zirzkee but interest from Italy has yet to materialise into anything concrete and he is expected to stay at the club.
summary: Manchester United suffered an opening-day Premier League defeat to Hull City, but there is no need to panic under Michael Carrick. The poor performance was largely attributed to a lack of match sharpness among key players and new signings, alongside Hull's well-drilled preparation. Looking ahead in the transfer window, United are unlikely to sign a new left-back before the deadline, relying instead on Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu, Noussair Mazraoui, and Diogo Dalot.
key_points: Michael Carrick's side lost their Premier League opening match to promoted Hull City.
Several key Manchester United players lacked match sharpness and full pre-season preparation.
Hull City was praised for being a well-drilled outfit with a fully prepared squad.
Manchester United have spent over £150m on midfield reinforcements but still face a gap at left-back.
The club is currently unlikely to sign a new left-back before the transfer window closes, placing pressure on Luke Shaw and other squad options.

title: Brydon Carse dropped by England as investigation begins into handcuffs incident
author: Ali Martin
content:
Brydon Carse has been stood down from England’s squad for the second Test against Pakistan this week as the footage of him in police handcuffs outside a bar in Derby city centre is investigated by the sport’s disciplinary body.
Carse was filmed by a member of the public while being spoken to by police officers outside Molly Malone’s Tavern on Saturday night, as Durham celebrated victory over Derbyshire in the County Championship earlier in the day.
The 31-year-old fast bowler is said to have been in handcuffs for “a few minutes” but was not arrested or charged. The former England captain, Ben Stokes, can be seen in the background of the footage shared on social media, while fast bowler Matthew Potts is seen speaking to security staff and police.
Though not officially on England duty – he had been released from the squad for the first Test in Leeds – Carse is a centrally-contracted player and now the matter is being looked into by the Cricket Regulator regarding a possible disrepute charge.
In the meantime, and in light of a string of late night drink-related incidents that have plagued the England men’s team over the past nine months, Carse has been dropped from the Test squad. Though part of the winter’s Ashes tour – England’s leading wicket-taker no less – Carse was not expected to play.
A statement from the England and Wales Cricket Board on Monday read: “Following a referral from the ECB, the Cricket Regulator have confirmed that they will investigate events on Saturday night in Derby. Brydon Carse will no longer be available for selection for the Second Men’s Rothesay Test Match while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained. Brydon will be replaced in the squad for this match by Sonny Baker.”
According to sources, the footage taken of Carse came after he was denied re-entry to the bar. He is understood to have earlier had “an exchange of words” with another member of the public inside regarding a spilled drink. Durham, though not his direct employers, are not believed to be pursuing the matter.
Carse was among a 15-man squad that was due to convene in London on Monday afternoon before the first of two training days at Lord’s ahead of the second Test that starts on Thursday. After going 1-0 up in the series, Joe Root has been presented with an early off-field headache in his second spell as captain.
Root, 35, had recently removed a team curfew that had been in place since last winter’s Ashes and a 4-1 defeat that was dogged by off-field stories regarding alcohol consumption. The Carse situation then arose just five days after Root told players to be “good human beings” in his first press conference back.
The decision to stand Carse down while the investigation takes place is in keeping with the precedent when Stokes and Gus Atkinson missed the second Test against New Zealand at the Oval in June following a late night incident in a bar in Chelsea after victory in the series opener at Lord’s.
The midnight curfew was in place on that occasion, even if it was later argued the precise details of it had not been well communicated. Atkinson was involved in a physical altercation with a Saracens rugby player – he was not the aggressor, as per the ECB – while Stokes was simply present at the same venue.
The ECB chose a different path on the eve of last winter’s Australia tour, however, when Harry Brook was punched by a nightclub bouncer on the eve of captaining a one-day international in Wellington, New Zealand. Brook was given a clandestine fine at the time, something which only came to light at the end of the Ashes.
summary: England fast bowler Brydon Carse has been dropped from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan while the Cricket Regulator investigates a video of him in police handcuffs outside a Derby bar. Carse was detained for a few minutes following an alleged dispute over a spilled drink and subsequent denial of re-entry to the venue, though he was not arrested or charged. The incident follows a series of alcohol-related off-field episodes involving the England team, prompting the ECB to remove him from selection pending full facts of the investigation.
key_points: Brydon Carse was stood down from the England Test squad after footage emerged of him in police handcuffs outside a Derby bar.
Carse was detained for a few minutes following an exchange over a spilled drink but was not arrested or charged.
The Cricket Regulator is investigating the incident for a possible disrepute charge, and Sonny Baker has replaced Carse in the squad.
Ben Stokes and Matthew Potts were also present at the scene, adding to recent off-field alcohol-related incidents surrounding the England team.

title: Enes Kanter Freedom ejected from WNBA game after verbal altercation with Natasha Cloud
author: Katie Falkingham
content:
![Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud argue](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1008/cpsprodpb/9787/live/8ac78650-9fa8-11f1-bff6-57f1422ebb0b.jpg)
Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud argue during the Chicago Sky's defeat
- Published
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday's Women's NBA match between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever after becoming involved in a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.
Sitting at courtside, Kanter Freedom stood up with his arms outstretched and took steps towards the court after Cloud began pointing and shouting at him during a timeout.
Kanter Freedom was wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with the words "WOMAN noun. Adult human female.".
Earlier this month, he declared he would enter next season's WNBA Draft, citing the current eligibility guidelines, or lack of, for transgender women players.
Security and other Sky players intervened, before former Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics centre Kanter Freedom was escorted from the court.
He posted on X, external: "I just got kicked out of a WNBA game for supporting WOMEN! Let that sink in, AMERICA!"
Writing on Threads, external after the game, Cloud said: "To every trans kid/person, you are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. You're loved. You're seen. You're perfect as you are & you will always be protected by me."
Kanter Freedom reportedly spoke with police officers before exiting Chicago's Wintrust Arena.
The Fever won the match 113-90.
"There's so many good things about this league and so many good things about the play of these players, that if you come to a game, you should probably come to enjoy the basketball," said Sky head coach Tyler Marsh.
"That seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that, too."
On Saturday, the Sky's win over Golden State Valkyries was one of two WNBA matches interrupted after sex toys were thrown on to the court.
There were similar incidents last season when six WNBA matches in Atlanta, New York and Los Angeles were interrupted.
USA Today, external reported the same group responsible for last year's incidents has said it will continue to disrupt WNBA games to protest against the league's policy on transgender athletes.
The WNBA operates under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), a deal negotiated between the league and its players association (WNBPA), setting rules on matters including player salary caps, revenue sharing, benefits and overall league operations.
On player eligibility, the CBA states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."
There are no transgender athletes currently competing in the league, but intense debate in the US has been sparked by recent comments from Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham - who played in Sunday's match in Chicago - questioning the current rules.
summary: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from a WNBA game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever following a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. Kanter Freedom, who sat courtside wearing a t-shirt defining the word "woman," was escorted out by security after stepping toward the court. Earlier this month, he stated he would enter the WNBA draft to protest transgender eligibility guidelines.
key_points: Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from a WNBA game after a verbal altercation with Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud.
Kanter Freedom wore a t-shirt featuring a definition of the word "woman" and had previously announced plans to enter the WNBA draft regarding transgender eligibility.
Natasha Cloud defended transgender individuals on social media following the incident.
The Indiana Fever defeated the Chicago Sky 113-90 in the match.

title: Hull City 2-0 Manchester United: Assistant Dean Holden on back five tactic
author: Charlotte Coates
content:
Highlights: Hull shock Manchester United on opening weekend
- Published
Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic kept his plan to topple Manchester United on the Tigers' Premier League return under wraps for weeks, assistant head coach Dean Holden told Match of the Day.
Jakirovic's side produced a sensational 2-0 opening-weekend win over Michael Carrick's side on Saturday while deploying a back five.
Hull were making their first Premier League appearance in nine years after coming up through the play-offs last season.
First-half goals from defenders Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy gave them their first league win over United since 1974.
Jakirovic altered his tactics for the game, having watched a couple of United's pre-season matches, including the 4-2 defeat by AC Milan, engineered by former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.
The Hull head coach repeatedly switched play to his wing-backs, which United's defence failed to cover.
When asked about the tactic, Holden told Match of the Day: "We certainly didn't copy Ruben Amorim.
"Serg had it in the back of his mind for three or four weeks that he was thinking of playing a back five. He didn't want to give anything away in pre-season, so we played a back four.
"The easiest thing to do in preparation was using some of the Milan clips, and Leeds the week before played a back three too, so that helped us with players where the systems looked similar."
Hull's win over United, who finished third in the Premier League last season, is perhaps even more remarkable given the Tigers only had 28% of possession.
But seeing limited amounts of the ball is not a cause for concern for Hull, says Holden.
"We are comfortable without the ball, so it is not like we are coming up here having dominated the Championship and now we have to change," said Holden.
"We are comfortable in that mid-block, that is one of our biggest strengths. Counter-attack as well.
"Sunderland set the trend with Leeds in terms of teams who have come up, and for us it is about belief.
"We have a group of lads who have done the hard yards, there is no real superstars in there.
"The manager is the same, very humble. Feet will be firmly on the ground."
Sergej Jakirovic post-match interview - Hull City v Manchester United
Jakirovic's Hull were favourites to finish bottom of the Premier League, having only squeezed into the play-offs on the final day of last season.
They became the first team to finish sixth and win the play-offs in 16 years - beating Middlesbrough in the final.
Just 15 months ago the Tigers had been close to being relegated to League One, only staying in the Championship on goal difference in 2024-25.
Three of the team who started their 1-1 draw against Portsmouth on the final day that secured their Championship status in that campaign were in the team which beat United.
Former Oldham Athletic, Bristol City and Charlton manager Holden joined the Tigers that summer and is now relishing a campaign in the top flight.
"We are aiming to stay in the league. It is the hardest thing to do and then you build on top of that," Holden said.
"But a win at home in the first game is beyond anyone's dreams really. The performance is the biggest thing, the confidence, the belief, will stand us in good stead."
summary: Hull City secured a sensational 2-0 victory against Manchester United on the opening weekend of the Premier League season using a surprise back-five tactic. Assistant head coach Dean Holden revealed that manager Sergej Jakirovic kept the tactical shift quiet for weeks in preparation for the match. First-half goals from defenders Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy sealed the historic win despite Hull holding only 28% possession.
key_points: Hull City defeated Manchester United 2-0 in their first Premier League match in nine years.
Manager Sergej Jakirovic secretly planned to use a back-five formation for weeks before the game.
First-half goals by Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy gave Hull their first league win over United since 1974.
Hull achieved the victory despite having only 28% possession, relying on a strong mid-block and counter-attacks.

title: Premier League title race: Liverpool and Man City nowhere near Arsenal's level, says Gary Neville
author: Gary Neville
content:
Premier League title race: Liverpool and Man City nowhere near Arsenal's level, says Gary Neville
Gary Neville predicts Manchester City and Liverpool will not challenge Arsenal this season for the Premier League title; Neville set to join Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football for Fulham vs Chelsea where the pair will reveal their season predictions with David Jones
Monday 24 August 2026 09:39, UK
Liverpool and Manchester City are well below the level required to win the Premier League title this season, says Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville.
City are entering the unknown after Pep Guardiola's departure, while Liverpool are rebuilding under Andoni Iraola.
A last-gasp Josko Gvardiol winner handed Enzo Maresca a 2-1 win in his first Premier League game in charge of City against Bournemouth and Liverpool also left it late to draw 2-2 with Newcastle.
Arsenal's opening win was far more straightforward, swatting aside Coventry City 3-0 with minimal fuss. With only one week gone, the Gunners are already odds-on with bookmakers to win the Premier League despite there being 37 games to go.

And Neville is struggling to see a situation where City or Liverpool challenge Arsenal this season.
Speaking on The Gary Neville Podcast, he said: "Last week when we were previewing the season, all I kept thinking about was that this is going to be the most unpredictable season. It's going to be intriguing because you've got new managers, you've got lots of new players, you've got so much change at the top.
"Arsenal should win this league by a street - and I don't sit here on Sunday evening thinking anything differently, we've seen Tottenham get beat, we've seen Manchester United get beat, we've seen Liverpool nearly get beat, we've seen City scrambling for a win at home, so everything we thought we would see, we're seeing. The unpredictable nature of teams at the top, probably not being good enough to go and basically do what they did last season and the season before and getting beat by teams that are well organised like Brentford and Hull and others.
"Man City are the same as Liverpool, these two clubs were getting nearly 100 points, six, seven years ago. Treble winners, four times Premier League winners, Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool, Arne Slot's champions, that's just happened and so we're measuring these two clubs by the standards that they've set, but they're nowhere near that standard.
"This Liverpool team are nowhere near the levels of a Premier League title winning team - they need a lot of work.
"I think they'll be happy with the point [vs Newcastle], a good finish for them, and they're celebrating, but I think deep down when you're measuring yourself and the standards that Liverpool have in the last five, 10 years of winning titles, I think they'll travel home, back to Liverpool and back to Merseyside, and they'll be thinking, we've got a lot of work to do.
"And Man City, they're well below where they need to be. Losing Rodri is a massive blow."
Nev 'so sure' Arsenal will win Premier League
With City and Liverpool lagging behind, Neville can see a situation where Chelsea could be Arsenal's closest rivals in the title race.
Xabi Alonso's men get their campaign off and running on Monday Night Football at Fulham, where Neville will be joining Jamie Carragher to reveal his season predictions.
Neville added: "Arsenal are going to be feeling really confident right now.
"It's the most sure I've ever been, and look it could be that I've got egg on my face at the end of the season, [but] it's the most sure I've ever been after game one that we're going to see a team be Premier League champions.
"Chelsea will finish second, unless I see them play really badly at Fulham, so I do reserve the right to change my opinion. I do think Chelsea will finish second because of the squad and because of the fact they haven't got European competition.
"They haven't got the confusion, they've got a good manager, so I do think Chelsea have got a great chance to push Arsenal this year and finish second and be the team and let's see on Monday night."
summary: Pundit Gary Neville believes that Manchester City and Liverpool are currently not at the level required to challenge for the Premier League title this season. Following the opening weekend of matches, Neville stated that Arsenal should comfortably win the league due to their strong start and the struggles of their rivals. He also suggested that Chelsea could emerge as Arsenal's closest challengers to finish second.
key_points: Gary Neville predicts that Manchester City and Liverpool will not challenge Arsenal for the Premier League title.
Arsenal opened their campaign with a straightforward 3-0 win against Coventry City.
Both Manchester City and Liverpool showed vulnerabilities in their opening matches, securing narrow and late results.
Neville believes Chelsea could finish second behind Arsenal due to their strong squad and lack of European competition.

title: Charles Leclerc reveals Ferrari instruction key to Lewis Hamilton unhappiness
author: Jake Nichol; Sàndor Mészáros
content:
![Leclerc Hamilton race Zandvoort](https://cdn.racingnews365.com/2026/Leclerc/XPB_1431772_HiRes.jpg?v=1787503614&width=1092&height=683&quality=85&crop=6000%2C3753%2C0%2C123)
Charles Leclerc has revealed how he was instructed to stay out by Ferrari during the sequence of events which left Lewis Hamilton frustrated in the Dutch Grand Prix.
Around half-distance, Hamilton closed up to the back of Leclerc on fresher tyres, having run long in the first stint after the red flag restart, and all but requested to be let through to continue his advance.
However, Leclerc was locked in an undercut/overcut battle with George Russell at the time, and initially appeared to disobey a team order to pit, and clear the path for Hamilton, with the Briton eventually getting past next time around when the Monegasque did pit.
Ultimately, Hamilton finished fourth, right on the tail of Russell for third, and felt the time lost behind Leclerc could have made the difference, but Leclerc has explained how he never got an order to cede position to Hamilton and was actually told to stay out, as he eventually finished in fifth, himself right behind Hamilton.
"These are the kind of choices that we need to speak of. For me, the thing that I want to look at is more the second stop actually, where we were pushing George to stop, and once he stopped, yes, Lewis was arriving, but two laps later I was requested to box," Leclerc explained to media, including RacingNews365s
"For me it was very important to create a tire delta to the Mercedes in order to come back strong at the end, and we didn't quite do that, so we need to look at why.
"I was very surprised to box so early when we had done exactly what we wanted. With George pitting, that was time for us to do five or 10, laps longer to build a tyre delta time to come back on the end at the end on George.
"Two laps later, I was told to box, which I did, I think three laps later.
"There wasn't much debate. I was asked to stop, and then towards the end of the lap, I was asked to stay on-track, which I did, and then the lap later, I was asked to stop.
"I didn't have any message on [on letting Hamilton past]. At the end of the day, I was focusing on my pace and trying to do the best I could for my race. I had a very good first stint. I had to stop early to try and undercut the guys in front, and that's a bit of a team game.
"Sometimes you've got to put yourself in a little bit of risk, especially in the first stint for that, and Lewis was very strong on the second stint, but it's the way it goes.
"So I think sometimes I'll be frustrated. Sometimes Lewis will be frustrated, but it's the way it is.
"It's one position for the team. It doesn't change anything, so it's not that I'm disappointed or feeling any kind of way about that; it just felt like the luck wasn't really on our side, with the virtual safety car timing not being less than ideal timing for us.
"But at the same time, it's the way it is. I felt like before the break, I had the luck a little bit by my side for two, three races, and sometimes you get to know the other side of the coin, which I did [in the Dutch GP]."

title: Football transfer rumours: Alvarez set for Arsenal after being booed at Atlético?
author: Will Unwin
content:
Booing Julián Alvarez during Atlético Madrid’s draw with Villarreal on Sunday has seemingly convinced the Argentinian forward to consider joining Arsenal in the window. The former Manchester City man has been kept out of the reaches of Barcelona, who may not have the funds to complete the signing, whereas the Gunners have plenty of cash to splash.
Alejandro Balde was left out of the Barcelona squad as they roared past Elche, as the Catalan club open the door for a move to Manchester United. A new left-back should solve all of the problems at Old Trafford, that’s for sure.
Jarrod Bowen has committed his future to West Ham, despite them being relegated and starting the Championship season in desperate fashion. Despite all that, perhaps he will be tempted by a £50m bid from Crystal Palace after a welcome to the Championship to forget? The Eagles were blunt at Everton over the weekend and could be about to initiate panic stations by splashing out quite severely for the Hammers skipper.
Losing 4-0 at Brighton is not going to do much for morale but it will make a team take drastic action in the market. Aston Villa have lined up Joel Ordóñez to solve all of their problems for the remainder of the season, if Club Brugge are willing to sell the centre-back.
There is only one way to bounce back from losing at Ipswich and that is to chase a £34m Barcelona player. Sunderland have tracked Marc Casadó throughout the summer and could be about to pounce for the 22-year-old, who has also been linked with most of the Premier League in recent weeks.
It is difficult to decipher if Cruzeiro’s Jonathan Jesus would sign for Strasbourg or Chelsea, but the talk in Brazil is that ownership group BlueCo want the 22-year-old centre-back. Real Betis, Valencia and Benfica are equally keen, adding a bit of jeopardy to the chase.
With Chelsea always looking to move on a few players, they will be ecstatic to hear that Napoli are contemplating a move for the striker Marc Guiu. Whether the Italians are up for splurging £25m on the Spaniard remains to be seen because the Serie A club currently believe the Blues’ valuation is a touch on the high side.
As alluded to, it was a fantastic start to the season for Hull on Saturday when they gave Manchester United a bit of a shooing. To help build on that, they have agreed a £15.4m deal to sign forward Mohamed-Ali Cho from Nice.
after newsletter promotion
And despite his goal against Liverpool, Joe Willock is being linked with a move to Besiktas, the Turkish club apparently casting flirtatious glances towards the Newcastle midfielder.
summary: Recent football transfer rumors highlight potential moves for several players following club matches and season openings. Notable developments include Julián Alvarez considering a move to Arsenal, Alejandro Balde being linked to Manchester United, and Jarrod Bowen attracting interest from Crystal Palace. Other clubs such as Aston Villa, Sunderland, and Hull are also pursuing targets to strengthen their squads.
key_points: Julián Alvarez is reportedly considering joining Arsenal after being booed by Atlético Madrid fans.
Barcelona's Alejandro Balde has been left out of the squad, opening the door for a potential move to Manchester United.
Crystal Palace is considering a £50m bid for West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen.
Hull has agreed to a £15.4m deal to sign forward Mohamed-Ali Cho from Nice.
Napoli is contemplating a £25m move for Chelsea striker Marc Guiu, though they currently consider the valuation high.

title: When will the penny finally drop for England’s cricketers?
author: Nick Hoult
content:
![Brydon Carse](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/cricket/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000497553092_17875173032340_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqNRyQPVJqXeAj80njYsdSlkpmpbPypFkbJ2gKT6wheOE.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Brydon Carse](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/cricket/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000497553092_17875173032340_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqNRyQPVJqXeAj80njYsdSlkpmpbPypFkbJ2gKT6wheOE.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Just 10 days after Joe Root dropped the England curfew, a member of the public filmed one of his players in police handcuffs outside a nightclub.
Taken on its own, the incident involving Brydon Carse in Derby on Saturday night sounds like something and nothing.
Insiders say it was a few verbals over a spilt drink with no physical altercation and all over in a matter of minutes, but when will they learn?
A police officer still felt it necessary to slap the cuffs on Carse, possibly in fear of his size and the potential for what could happen rather than what did happen. He was released a few minutes later once it all calmed down, but not before it was filmed on a camera phone and was being bandied around WhatsApp groups in professional cricket within a few hours.
It is at least an opportunity for Root to stamp his authority and Carse will be a worried man. “My view on curfews is that I don’t think they work and if you want guys to take responsibility on the field, they’ve got to feel like they can be grown adults off it and make good, strong decisions off it,” Root said in his first interview when he was reappointed captain. This was not a good, strong decision by Carse and the noise around the England team, which had died down with the win at Headingley, is suddenly raised again.
He was released from the England squad at Headingley to play for Durham in the County Championship. Nobody has a problem with him and his team-mates celebrating a win over Derbyshire, but Carse is in the squad for the second Test at Lord’s this week and, in the current climate, the behaviour of England’s cricketers is under scrutiny like never before.
If an official at the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) a year ago had wargamed worst-case scenarios and presented them to the board, they would have been laughed at for an overactive imagination for coming up with the following chain of events:
- Harry Brook would be punched by a bouncer the night before captaining England and then publicly apologise for lying about the fact two team-mates were with him;
- The team would go on a bender in Noosa at 2-0 down in the Ashes and Ben Duckett would be filmed legless, asking people the way to the hotel;
- The management would slap a curfew on the team, only for the captain Ben Stokes and bowler Gus Atkinson to break it after the first Test of the summer;
- A punch would be thrown at Atkinson by a professional rugby player and Stokes would eventually retire over the incident;
- Root would then be reappointed, drop the curfew and 10 days later the police would put cuffs on one of his bowlers.
Carse was in the thick of the drinking on the Ashes tour and must know anyone getting in trouble would be on shaky ground with Root and a new head coach, Stephen Fleming, who will be more schoolmasterly than his predecessor. The players could generally count on the support of Brendon McCullum, who had a few scrapes in his time and was aware young men can do silly things. They do not know how Fleming will react; he has no loyalty to these players and it will be easier for him to remove anyone he thinks could be a problem than it was for McCullum, who had made Carse one of his leading bowlers and picked him for every Ashes Test last winter.
![Carse (left) with England team-mates Harry Brook (centre) and Will Jacks during the infamous trip to Noosa last winter](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/cricket/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000455624046_17874959584600_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqcckId3_uTHSCNPmH5K41OlHwtdpQwyNje2OyIL7x97s.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
For the ECB, it is an awful look for one of its players to be in police handcuffs in this climate, but it has reacted this time with a bit more restraint than it did over the Stokes-Atkinson incident. Then it rushed to judgment too quickly because it was still bruised over the Brook saga, which was kept internal in the hope it would never be made public.
Carse remains part of the squad for the Lord’s Test, pending an internal team investigation by the England management. The Cricket Regulator has been informed and, if it decides to launch its own investigation, then Carse will be removed from the squad for Thursday’s match.
He was unlikely to play at Lord’s anyway, but is probably the first choice if one of the attack pulls out with injury. Carse has not played Test cricket since the Ashes, because of injury, and with Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue, Jofra Archer and Atkinson looking a potent combination at Headingley, he had slipped down the pecking order.
Root wants them to act like grown-ups. There are plenty of blokes Carse’s age, 31, who will have had a scrape with the law this weekend outside a city-centre pub, but not with their employer and boss (Root) explicitly telling them to stay out of trouble. It is unfortunate, from Carse’s point of view, that he was filmed, but then again it is a reminder of two things.
First, there are cameras everywhere, which makes it even more important not to attract attention. Secondly, eyes are on the players because of their reputation. This has only added to it.
summary: England cricketer Brydon Carse was filmed in police handcuffs outside a Derby nightclub following a verbal disagreement over a spilt drink, just 10 days after captain Joe Root removed team curfews to encourage player responsibility. Carse was released after a few minutes and remains in the squad for the upcoming Lord's Test pending an internal investigation, though the Cricket Regulator has also been informed. The incident places renewed scrutiny on the England team's off-field behavior following a series of recent disciplinary controversies.
key_points: Brydon Carse was briefly handcuffed by police outside a Derby nightclub after a verbal altercation involving a spilt drink.
The incident occurred only 10 days after captain Joe Root lifted team curfews in favor of trusting players to act responsibly.
Carse remains in the squad for the second Test at Lord's pending an internal investigation and potential review by the Cricket Regulator.
The event adds to a string of recent off-field controversies involving England cricketers, drawing intense public and media scrutiny.

title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal medical, Alvarez twist; new Man Utd boost
author: George Flood; Tashan Deniran-Alleyne
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/24/5/25/bradleybarcolajulianalvarezalejandrobalde.jpeg?trim=0,0,75,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=1000)
The summer window is set for a lively finish as Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Tottenham and Liverpool all push for further signings before the deadline. Arsenal continue to chase a deal for Julian Alvarez, who is apparently open to a Premier League return. The Gunners also remain interested in the likes of Victor Osimhen, Kenan Yildiz and Matias Fernandez-Pardo as Gabriel Martinelli heads for the exit, while they could swoop for Eli Junior Kroupi in January. Igor Tyjon has undergone an Arsenal medical and should be followed by Manchester United duo James Scanlon and Habeeb Ogunneye.
Manchester United will announce the signing of Carlos Baleba and have been boosted over Alejandro Balde as they weigh up a big offer for Lewis Hall, while Chelsea are focused on exits but could move for Francisco Conceicao if Pedro Neto leaves. Liverpool remain in talks over Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye as they plot a third bid for Yankuba Minteh, having made a shock Endrick enquiry.
Latest transfer news and rumours
Live updates
Arsenal ponder bid for Matias Fernandez-Pardo
Arsenal are also said to hold a growing interest in Matias Fernandez-Pardo.
The highly-rated Belgian attacker is expected to follow the Manchester City-bound Ayyoub Bouaddi out of Lille before the summer transfer deadline.
Liverpool and Manchester United have been linked with Fernandez-Pardo, who was subject to a bid from RB Leipzig over the weekend and has interest from Marseille.
According to Sebastien Denis of French outlet Foot Mercato, the 21-year-old is on Arsenal’s shortlist as they monitor the situation very closely, though would need to offer around €70m (£60m) in order to convince Lille to sell.
Julian Alvarez to Arsenal latest
More now on Arsenal’s well-documented pursuit of Julian Alvarez.
Transfer specialist Ben Jacobs has been on talkSPORT, reporting that Arsenal will move for the wantaway Atletico Madrid striker if they are given any encouragement in the coming days.
He insists the door is not 100 per cent shut on Alvarez potentially joining Arsenal, with sporting director Andrea Berta alert to the possibility.
However, Jacobs says that outgoings are key if the Gunners are to pull off a late transfer of that magnitude amid ongoing talks with Al-Hilal over Gabriel Martinelli.
Man City to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi and Allan
Manchester City also look to have wrapped up another couple of signings in their late summer transfer drive.
The FA Cup holders were confirmed over the weekend to have finally agreed a deal with Lille for Moroccan midfield sensation Ayyoub Bouaddi worth an initial €95m (£81.3m), plus €5m (£4.2m) in add-ons.
Fabrizio Romano says that Bouaddi will fly to England on Monday in order to undergo a medical and sign a five-year contract at the Etihad Stadium.
His arrival comes as Newcastle reportedly make significant strides towards a deal for Nico Gonzalez.
City are also said to be replacing the Tottenham-bound Savinho with fellow Brazilian attacker Allan, who will join from Palmeiras for around €40m (£34.2m).
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/24/07/01M07T544DNYR5MCH1C3STN78W.jpg?trim=112,0,112,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=640)
Man Utd to announce Carlos Baleba signing
Manchester United should announce the signing of Carlos Baleba today.
The Cameroon midfielder underwent a medical and signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford over the weekend.
That was after United finally agreed a deal with Brighton for their long-term transfer target on Friday evening worth an initial £65m, plus a further £5m in add-ons.
Brighton are understood to have also inserted a sell-on clause into the deal.
Baleba is not expected to make his United debut until around mid-September due to an ankle ligament injury suffered during pre-season.
Liverpool get new Bradley Barcola hope
Paris Saint-Germain have hinted that Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye could still leave the club before the summer transfer deadline amid ongoing talks with Liverpool.
Both players were left out of the PSG squad again by head coach Luis Enrique for yesterday’s opening Ligue 1 clash at Rennes as Liverpool continue negotiations over a high-profile double deal.
Speaking during the coverage of that game, PSG advisor Luis Campos suggested that Barcola and Mbaye could follow the example of Gianluigi Donnarumma last year and leave very late in the window.
“The transfer window isn’t over at all,” he said.
“Even with incoming transfers, if we find a good opportunity, we’re going to go for it.
“In terms of departures, we’ll see what happens regarding Barcola and Mbaye.
“I understand your questions about them but you also have to understand my position.
“We’ll see what happens at the end of the window, remember last year with Donnarruma it was done at the end of the window. We’ll see.”
Tottenham agree Omar Marmoush loan deal
Omar Marmoush will undergo a medical at Tottenham today.
Spurs have been pursuing the signing of the Manchester City striker after wrapping up a deal for team-mate Savinho that could be worth as much as £85m.
Fabrizio Romano reports that there is now a verbal agreement in place between the two clubs for Marmoush to join Tottenham on an initial season-long loan that contains the option for a £50m permanent transfer next summer.
The Egyptian international is expected to have a medical and sign a contract in north London on Monday.
Arsenal eye Eli Junior Kroupi move
Could Eli Junior Kroupi yet provide the transfer answer for Arsenal in attack this season?
The French forward looked likely to move on this summer after a fine first season in the Premier League at Bournemouth, with Tottenham also among the clubs said to be keen on his signature.
However, any chance of a high-profile switch was scuppered by a foot injury suffered at a pre-season training camp in Austria in July that required surgery and was expected to keep him sidelined for three to four months.
A move could still be on the cards in January though if that injury heals as expected, with HandofArsenal insisting that he is a target to watch for many clubs in the mid-season window - including the Gunners.
Man Utd handed Alejandro Balde boost
All roads could yet be leading to Manchester United for Alejandro Balde.
We’ve already mentioned this morning that Hansi Flick is planning to hold more talks with the Spanish left-back today after he left him out of his squad for Sunday’s LaLiga opener against Elche, feeling that he was not 100 per cent focused and needed to clear his mind amid the ongoing transfer speculation.
Flick denied that he had told Balde to leave, saying he has asked the player to think about his future before resuming discussions on Monday.
Catalan publication Sport claim that Balde has given the green light to agent Jorge Mendes to find him a new club following an initial approach from Manchester United made last week.
Barcelona are said to be looking for a fee of around £38m for the 22-year-old, who has spoken favourably about United in the past.
Martinelli absence explained as Arsenal hold talks for £60m transfer
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has already explained why Gabriel Martinelli has not featured in any of his matchday squads this season, as Al Hilal reportedly pursue a deal for the Brazilian.
After a surprise omission against Manchester City in the Community Shield, eyebrows were raised once again when the Gunners began the defence of their Premier League crown on Friday night against newly-promoted Coventry City.
Although Arteta made two changes to the side that started at Wembley, with Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka replacing Bruno Guimaraes and Noni Madueke, there was to be no recall for Martinelli.
The forward was one of several senior players left out of the matchday squad, along with Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira and Reiss Nelson.
There are no suggestions that Martinelli is injured, rather his omission is down to Premier League rules stipulating that teams are only to name a 20-player squad on matchdays, a ruling that Arteta has requested changes.
New Julian Alvarez to Arsenal transfer twist
The Julian Alvarez transfer saga rumbles on, with Arsenal clearly not giving up hope.
It was reported by Diario AS in Spain over the weekend that Alvarez was now leaving the door open to a potential return to the Premier League before the transfer deadline following more talks with Mikel Arteta as he still desperately attempts to leave Atletico Madrid.
Alvarez missed the first game of the new LaLiga season but returned against Villarreal yesterday, coming off the bench in the second half to jeers and loud whistles from an Atletico crowd angry at his public desire to join Barcelona.
He was kept away from fans at the end of the game and had a scarf thrown at him as he walked down the tunnel at the Metropolitano Stadium, with his facial expressions and body language again becoming a huge talking point on social media.
Journalist Nicolo Schira is now reporting that Barcelona will make a new attempt to sign Alvarez this week. Will Arsenal follow suit?
summary: Major Premier League clubs are making late moves in the summer transfer window, with Arsenal pursuing players like Julian Alvarez and Matias Fernandez-Pardo while managing potential outgoings. Manchester United is set to announce the signing of Carlos Baleba and is linked with Alejandro Balde, whereas Manchester City has reportedly agreed deals for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Allan. Meanwhile, Tottenham has reached a verbal agreement for a loan deal for Omar Marmoush, and Liverpool remains in talks over Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.
key_points: Arsenal is closely monitoring Julian Alvarez and considering a bid for Lille attacker Matias Fernandez-Pardo.
Manchester United is expected to announce the £65m signing of midfielder Carlos Baleba.
Manchester City agreed a deal worth an initial €95m with Lille for Ayyoub Bouaddi.
Tottenham has a verbal agreement to sign Manchester City striker Omar Marmoush on an initial season-long loan with an option to buy.
PSG suggested that Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye could leave the club before the transfer deadline amidst interest from Liverpool.

title: FPL notes: Iraola on Szoboszlai pen + Wissa back to his best
author: Avfc
content:
Liverpool somehow salvaged a point at St James’ Park on Sunday, thanks to a late penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai (£7.0m).
Here are our Scout Notes from the game.
- READ MORE: FPL Gameweek 1: Sunday’s goals, assists, bonus + DefCon points
- READ MORE: FPL notes: De Cuyper + Hinshelwood haul, Villa injury latest
![The Only FPL Companion App You Need for 2026/27 1](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-2026-07-24T120104.598.jpg)
SZOBOSZLAI PEN
Szoboszlai, not Alexander Isak (£9.0m), smashed in a late penalty to rescue a draw for Liverpool.
Buried into the top corner, the £7.0m midfielder really couldn’t have placed his spot-kick any better.
“I was practising a lot in the pre-season, obviously we didn’t have any [penalties during the friendly games], but in training, so thanks to the second and third goalies to be there for me.” – Dominik Szoboszlai
A pressure penalty – have we got our answer about who steps up from 12 yards after Mohamed Salah’s departure?
Or was Isak perhaps spared the pressure on his return to St James’ Park?
Andoni Iraola later said…
“I think we have not only Dom [Szoboszlai] and Alexander [Isak] – we have more very good specialists. Alexis [Mac Allister] also was on the pitch and he’s a very good penalty-taker, Cody [Gakpo] – we have a lot. But I think Dom showed the level. It’s an almost impossible penalty to stop.” – Andoni Iraola
Decisive from the spot, Szoboszlai also had complete control over Liverpool’s set plays, taking all of the Reds’ corners and free-kicks.
Prior to his late equaliser, Cody Gakpo (£7.0m) found the bottom corner with a lovely drilled finish from outside the box.
The Dutchman racked up six shots on Sunday, the most of any player in Gameweek 1 so far, and later hit the defensive contribution (DefCon) threshold to total 12 points.
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-366.png)
Above: Players sorted by shots in Gameweek 1, via our Stats Centre Page
ISAK + WIRTZ POOR
On his return to St James’ Park, Isak didn’t really show up.
Liverpool had 27 shots in this match, with the Sweden international involved in five of them either as the shot taker or creator.
But in front of a hostile crowd, it was a game of frustration for the most part, with a header blocked and an effort blazed over the bar from just inside the box.
“I think he expected a little bit the atmosphere, I don’t think [it] has been a big surprise for him. I think he has tried everything, has given us good positions on the ball. [He] probably has had a couple of situations to finish inside the box, but probably not the clearest that he wanted or we wanted, but I value that. He has continued pushing on in the game, fighting, and I think it’s a good step for Alex for being the first game.” – Andoni Iraola on Alexander Isak
Florian Wirtz (£7.5m), who played as part of a front two with Isak, was equally poor and hooked just after the hour mark, although he was denied by a decent early save from Lukas Hornicek (£5.0m).
Others in red disappointed, too, including both full-backs and Rio Ngumoha (£6.0m), who didn’t look comfortable at all down the right flank. His replacement, Victor Munoz (£6.0m), fared better and won the late penalty.
Defensively, Liverpool didn’t fill you with much confidence, but Jeremy Jacquet (£5.0m) generally did well before his removal in the 70th minute.
“Jeremy [Jacquet] hasn’t done a proper pre-season, so it was kind of expected he didn’t finish the game.
“All the substitutes gave us energy. We need it because it’s difficult to last the full 90 minutes with the same players the way we want to play. Players coming off the bench can affect the game.” – Andoni Iraola
WISSA SUPERB
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-23T171734Z_2125986550_UP1EM8N1C19AN_RTRMADP_3_SOCCER-ENGLAND-NEW-LIV-1-1024x452.jpg)
Although they dropped two points late on, this was a really positive performance from Newcastle under new boss Matthias Jaissle.
Anthony Elanga (£6.0m) and substitute Joe Willock (£5.0m) got the goals, but Yoane Wissa (£6.0m) was the clear standout performer.
Yes, he missed a couple of big chances, but he linked up very well with Will Osula (£6.0m) from a No 10 role (see image below), looked sharp throughout and carried the ball superbly to set up Willock’s strike.
“With the new role he’s given me it’s given me a lot of confidence. I’m one of the leaders so I need to back him. Because on the pitch you can’t always hear him so I need to make sure the guys are on alert.
“The manager expects me to be a leader and lead the group. He wants me to be winning balls, making sure everyone is going forward, going for the kill, and sometimes just be calm. He wants me to keep up the energy. He wants a lot of energy and that’s the role he gave to me and I am very happy.” – Yoane Wissa on Matthias Jaissle
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Screen-Shot-2026-08-24-at-00.34.45-623x1024.png)
On this evidence, Wissa will cause plenty of problems for Tottenham Hotspur next weekend.
Indeed, both Newcastle goals on Sunday came from fast breaks, so Spurs will need to be really switched on to balls played in behind.
Elsewhere, Hornicek and Amar Dedic (£4.5m) both looked solid at the back.
Lewis Miley (£5.5m) impressed in the middle of the park, too, particularly after a limited pre-season.
BURN INJURY
Newcastle captain Dan Burn (£5.0m) is set to miss the next few weeks with an ankle injury suffered in training.
The England international had been in contention to face Liverpool but was spotted arriving at St James’ Park on crutches and wearing a protective boot.
A quick word on Osula, too.
He seemed to be struggling after a collision but battled on before finally coming off in the 56th minute.
We haven’t spotted an update thus far, although Newcastle play West Bromwich Albion in the EFL Cup in midweek, so we might hear something in Jaissle’s pre-match presser.
![](https://cdn.fantasyfootballscout.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Dont-Chase-Last-Weeks-Points.jpg)
summary: Liverpool salvaged a late draw against Newcastle thanks to a top-corner penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai after Cody Gakpo had earlier equalised. Despite Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz struggling in attack, Szoboszlai also took complete control of Liverpool's set pieces. For Newcastle, Yoane Wissa put in a standout performance to help his side secure a positive result under new manager Matthias Jaissle.
key_points: Dominik Szoboszlai scored a late penalty into the top corner to rescue a draw for Liverpool and took all of their corners and free-kicks.
Cody Gakpo recorded six shots and scored a drilled finish from outside the box, totaling 12 points.
Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz both had poor outings in Liverpool's attack during the match at St James' Park.
Yoane Wissa was the standout performer for Newcastle, providing sharp link-up play and carrying the ball to set up a goal for Joe Willock.
Newcastle captain Dan Burn is set to miss the next few weeks due to an ankle injury sustained in training.
